label: thm:equivalence
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:equivalence}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a locally finitely generated Grothendieck category with a generator $U$.
The following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a covering class.
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a precovering class.
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a special covering class.
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a special precovering class.
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under all small filtered colimits.
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under arbitrary coproducts.
\item $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under $|\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal A}(U)|$-indexed coproducts.
\item $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian and the following canonical inclusion has a right adjoint
\[
 K_{\mathrm{tac}}(\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A)\longrightarrow K(\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A).
\]
\end{enumerate}

label: lem:finite-endomorphism-generator
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:finite-endomorphism-generator}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck category with a generator $U$ whose endomorphism ring is finite.
Then $\mathcal A$ is equivalent to the category of modules over a finite ring.
In particular, $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian and $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a covering class.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $B=\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal A}(U)$.
Since $\mathcal{A}$ is a Grothendieck category with a generator $U$, one has a fully faithful functor $H=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(U,-):\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Mod}_B$ with an exact left adjoint $Q$ \cite[Theorem~2.5.2]{Krause2022}.
Moreover, By \cite[Proposition~2.2.11 and Lemma~2.2.10]{Krause2022},
there is a localisation sequence of abelian categories
\[
\xymatrix@C=2cm{
\ker Q
  \ar@<0.7ex>@{..>>}[r]+L;[]+R
& \mathrm{Mod}_B
  \ar@<0.7ex>@{>->}[l]+R+<0.5em,0pt>;[]+L
  \ar@<0.7ex>@{>->}[r]+L+<-0.5em,0pt>;[]+R^{H}
& \mathcal A
  \ar@<0.7ex>@{->>}[l]+R;[]+L^{Q}
}
\]
Since $B$ is artinian, the Serre subcategory $\ker Q$ corresponds to an idempotent $e\in B$ such that $\ker Q$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{Mod}_{B/BeB}$ \cite[Example~2.2.19(2)]{Krause2022}.
In this case $\mathcal{A}$ is equivalent to $\mathrm{Mod}_{eBe}$, which is a module category over a finite ring.
By \cite[Corollary~4.13]{Yu2016}, Gorenstein injective modules form a covering class over every Artin algebra, so $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a covering class.
This completes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:cardinal-coproducts
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cardinal-coproducts}
Let $\mathcal A$ be a locally finitely generated Grothendieck category. If every countable coproduct $E=\coprod_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n$ of injective objects $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is Gorenstein injective, then $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Take $E_n$'s and $E$ as in the statement.
By assumption, $E$ is Gorenstein injective.
Hence a complete injective resolution yields an injective precover $p : I\to E$.
Thus for each structure morphism $\iota_n : E_n \hookrightarrow E$, there is a lift $f_n : E_n \to I$ such that $p f_n = \iota_n$.
It follows that $E$ is a direct summand of $I$, and hence injective.
Since $\mathcal A$ is locally finitely generated, it follows from \cite[Theorem~11.2.12]{Krause2022} that $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian.
head: environment

label: lem:precovering-noetherian
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For a countable family of injective objects $(E_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$, take a Gorenstein injective precover $G\to E=\coprod_{n\in\mathbb N}E_n$ and an injective precover $I\to G$ from a complete injective resolution.
Let $p:I\to E$ denote such a composition.
For each structure morphism $\iota_n:E_n\to E$, there is a lift $f_n:E_n\to I$ such that $p f_n=\iota_n$.
It follows that $E$ is a direct summand of $I$, and hence injective.
Lemma~\ref{lem:cardinal-coproducts} shows that $\mathcal{A}$ is locally Noetherian.
head: environment

label: prop:noetherian-reduction
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:noetherian-reduction}
If any of conditions~\textup{(1)--(7)} of Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence} holds, then $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal A}(U)$ is finite, apply Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-endomorphism-generator}.
Suppose now that this ring is infinite.
Conditions~\textup{(1)--(4)} imply that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ forms a precovering class, so Lemma~\ref{lem:precovering-noetherian} applies.
Conditions~\textup{(5)--(7)} imply that countable coproducts of injective objects are in $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:cardinal-coproducts} applies.
This completes the proof.
head: environment

label: lem:gi-precover
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:gi-precover}
  For each $X \in \mathcal{A}$, denote the evaluation
  \[
  \epsilon_X : P(X) = \coprod_{E \in \mathcal{E}} \coprod_{f \in \mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(E,X)} E \to X
  \]
  Then for each $G \in \mathcal{GI}(\mathcal{A})$, the short exact sequence $0 \to \ker \epsilon_G \to P(G) \xrightarrow{\epsilon _G} G \to 0$ remains exact after applying $\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(E,-)$ for each $E \in \mathcal{E}$, and $\ker \epsilon_G \in \mathcal{GI}(\mathcal{A})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathcal{A}$ is locally Noetherian, $P(X)$ is a well-defined injective object for each $X \in \mathcal{A}$.
  By decomposition of injective objects, $\epsilon_X$ is an injective precover.
  For each $G \in \mathcal{GI}(\mathcal{A})$, choose a short exact sequence $0 \to G' \to E' \to G \to 0$ from a complete injective resolution of $G$.
  The map $E'\to G$ is an injective precover by \eqref{eq:gi-ext-vanishing}, which factors through $\epsilon_G$.
  Hence $\epsilon_G$ is epic.
  Then Schanuel lemma \cite[Lemma~2.2]{EJO2001} gives $G' \oplus P(G) \cong E' \oplus \ker \epsilon_G$.
  Thus $\ker \epsilon_G \in \mathcal{GI}(\mathcal{A})$.
  The short exact sequence $0 \to \ker \epsilon_G \to P(G) \xrightarrow{\epsilon _G} G \to 0$ remains exact after applying $\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(E,-)$ for each $E \in \mathcal{E}$.
head: environment

label: lem:gi-preenvelope
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $X \in \mathcal{A}$, since $J$ is a cogenerator and $\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(\iota_X, J)$ is surjective, $\iota_X$ is monic.
  By the dual procedure in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:gi-precover}, $\mathrm{coker} \iota_G$ is a summand of a Gorenstein injective object, and hence Gorenstein injective.
  Since $G \in \mathcal{GI}(\mathcal{A})$, the short exact sequence $0 \to G \xrightarrow{\iota_G} \prod_{\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(G,J)}J \to \mathrm{coker} \iota_G \to 0$ remains exact after applying $\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(E,-)$ for each $E \in \mathcal{E}$.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{lem:gi-basic}
There is a functor $\mathbf I:\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)$ whose values are totally acyclic complexes of injective objects, with a natural isomorphism $Z^0\mathbf I\cong\mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)}$.

title: Proof
body_md: For each $G \in \mathcal{GI}(\mathcal{A})$, construct a complete injective resolution $\mathbf I(G)$ by iterating the constructions in Lemmas~\ref{lem:gi-precover} and \ref{lem:gi-preenvelope} on the kernel and cokernel sides, respectively.

title: Remark
body_md: Note that this functor is not required to be additive in the further study.

label: lem:localizing-colimit
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $X=\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}T_d$ the colimit in $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)$.
Since $\mathcal{A}$ is locally Noetherian, the injective objects are closed under filtered colimits \cite[Theorem~11.2.12]{Krause2022}.
Thus $X \in \mathrm{Ch}(\mathrm{Inj}\mathcal{A})$.
The canonical maps $T_d\to X$ induce a compatible family of morphisms of dg module $\Phi (T_d)\to\Phi(X)$, and hence a comparison map $\alpha:\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}\Phi (T_d)\to\Phi(X)$.

For $N\in\mathcal N$ and a complex $Y$ of injective objects, the injective resolution $N\to iN$ yields a quasi-isomorphism $r_{N,Y}:\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(iN,Y)\to\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(N,Y)$ is a quasi-isomorphism: its $n$th cohomology map is
$\mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(iN,Y[n])\to\mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(N,Y[n])$, which is an isomorphism by \cite[Lemma~2.1]{Krause2005} for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.
Naturality in $Y$ gives the commutative diagram of complexes of abelian groups
\[
\xymatrix@C=2.5em@R=2em{
 \mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(iN,T_d)
 \ar[r]^-{\alpha(iN)}\ar[d]_-{\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}(r_{N,T_d})}
 &\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(iN,X)\ar[d]^{r_{N,X}}\\
 \mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(N,T_d)
 \ar[r]_-{\beta_N}^-{\sim}
 &\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}^{\bullet}(N,X).
}
\]
Since $N$ is finitely presented, $\beta_N$ is an isomorphism.
Recall that $r_{N,X}$ and each $r_{N, T_d}$ are quasi-isomorphisms.
By exactness of filtered colimits, $\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}(r_{N,T_d})$ is a quasi-isomorphism.
It follows that $\alpha(iN)$ is a quasi-isomorphism for every $N\in\mathcal N$, hence $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism of dg modules.

Now choose a projective cofibrant diagram replacement $q:Q \Phi (T)\twoheadrightarrow \Phi (T)$.
Each component $q_d$ is a quasi-isomorphism of dg modules.
Since filtered colimits of dg modules are computed objectwise and preserve quasi-isomorphisms, $\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}q_d$ is also a quasi-isomorphism.
Since $\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}(Q\Phi (T))_d$ represents $\mathrm{hocolim}_D \Phi (T)$, we obtain
\[
 \mathrm{hocolim}_D \Phi (T)
 \cong\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}(Q\Phi (T))_d
 \xlongrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}\Phi(T_d)
 \xlongrightarrow[\sim]{\alpha}\Phi(X)
 \qquad\text{in }D(\mathcal C).
\]
Applying the chosen quasi-inverse $\Phi^{-1}$ completes the proof.

label: lem:localising-hocolimits
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathcal M$ is combinatorial, it is cofibrantly generated. 
Thus the diagram category $\mathcal M^D$ admits the projective model structure, i.e., $\mathrm{Weq}$ and $\mathrm{Fib}$ are degreewise defined and $\mathrm{Cof} = {}^{\square}(\mathrm{Fib}\cap\mathrm{Weq})$ \cite[Theorem~11.6.1]{Hirschhorn2003}.

Suppose first that $\mathcal M$ is simplicial.
Take a projectively cofibrant diagram replacement $q:QF\to F$ in $\mathcal M^D$.
Each $(QF)_d$ is cofibrant, and $q_d$ is a weak equivalence, so $(QF)_d$ still represents an object of $\mathcal S$.
Since $\mathcal S$ is closed under coproducts, cones and extensions, \cite[Proposition~3.4]{CGR2014} applies and gives $\mathrm{hocolim}_D F\cong\mathrm{hocolim}_D QF\in\mathcal S$.

In general, by \cite[Proposition~3.1]{CGR2014}, $\mathcal{M}$ is Quillen equivalent to some stable simplicial combinatorial model category $\mathcal N$, i.e., $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:R$ is a Quillen equivalence with $L$ left adjoint.
Hence one has the triangle equivalence $\Psi = \mathbf L L:\mathsf{Ho}(\mathcal M) \xlongrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf{Ho}(\mathcal N)$.
By \cite[Theorem~11.6.5]{Hirschhorn2003}, this induces equivalences $\Psi_D:\mathsf{Ho}(\mathcal M^D)\xlongrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf{Ho}(\mathcal N^D)$, where the diagram categories carry their projective model structures.
Since $\Psi$ preserves triangles and coproducts, $\mathcal S'=\Psi(\mathcal S)$ is localising.
Take a cofibrant replacement $QF\to F$ in $\mathcal M^D$.
Set $F'=L^D(QF)$ and $F'_d=L((QF)_d)$.
Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Psi(\mathrm{hocolim}_D F)& = (\mathbf L L)(\mathrm{hocolim}_D F)\cong(\mathbf L L)(\mathrm{colim}_D QF) \cong L(\mathrm{colim}_D QF)\\
&\cong\mathrm{colim}_D(L^D QF)=\mathrm{colim}_D F'\cong\mathrm{hocolim}_D F' \in \mathcal{S}'.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here $\mathrm{colim}_D$ and $L^D$ are left Quillen, $\mathrm{colim}_D QF$ and $F'$ are cofibrant in $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal N^D$, respectively.
Since $\Psi$ is an equivalence, one has $\mathrm{hocolim}_D F\in\mathcal S$.

label: cor:localizing-colimit
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The projective model structure $\mathcal M$ for dg modules is stable, with suspension given by the shift.
$\mathcal{M}$ is also combinatorial, since it is cofibrantly generated, and the Grothendieck category of dg modules is locally presentable \cite[Proposition~3.10]{Beke2000}.
The triangulated equivalence $\Phi$ preserves coproducts, so $\Phi(\mathcal L)$ is localising in $D(\mathcal C)$.
Proposition~\ref{lem:localizing-colimit} and Lemma~\ref{lem:localising-hocolimits} give
\[
 \Phi\!\left(\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}T_d\right)
 \cong\mathrm{hocolim}_{d\in D}\Phi(T_d)\in\Phi(\mathcal L).
\]
Since $\Phi$ is an equivalence and $\mathcal L$ is closed under isomorphisms, $\mathrm{colim}_{d\in D}T_d\in\mathcal L$.

label: prop:card-criterion
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:card-criterion}
  Each indecomposable injective object $E$ is a quotient of a coproduct of at most $\kappa$ Noetherian subobjects of $U$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be the Noetherian subobjects of $U$; they form a generating family since their directed union is $U$.
Choose a nonzero Noetherian subobject $B_0\subseteq E$.
We construct $B_n$ inductively for each $n \in \mathbb N_+$.
When $B_n$ is constructed, put
\[
\Omega_n=\{(i,S,f)\mid i\in I,\ S\subseteq U_i,\ f:S\to B_n\}.
\]
Since $E$ is injective, for each $f : S \to B_n$ with $S \subseteq U_i$ one can fix an extension $\widetilde f : U_i \to E$. 
This defines $B_{n+1}=B_n+\sum_{(i,S,f)\in\Omega_n}\mathrm{Im}\,\widetilde f$.

We claim that $E=\bigcup_{n<\omega}B_n$.
Since $S\subseteq U_i$ is Noetherian, every map $f:S\to\bigcup_{n<\omega}B_n$ factors through some $B_n$ and hence extends over $U_i$ with image in $B_{n+1}$.
The proof of Baer's criterion, applied to the generating family $(U_i)$, makes $\bigcup_{n<\omega}B_n$ injective \cite[\S1.10, Lemme~1, p.~136]{Grothendieck1957}.
Its inclusion in $E$ therefore splits; since it contains $B_0\ne0$ and $E$ is indecomposable, $\bigcup_{n<\omega}B_n=E$.

It remains to show that $|\Omega_n| \leq \kappa$ for each $n \in \mathbb N$.
We claim that
\begin{enumerate}
  \item The collection of Noetherian subobjects of $U$ has cardinality at most $\kappa$,
  \item For Noetherian objects $M$ and $N$, one has $|\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,N)|\leq\kappa$.
\end{enumerate}
Indeed, each Noetherian subobject $U_i$ of $U$ is a quotient of finite coproducts of $U$, and hence $|I|$ is bounded by $|\mathrm{End}_\mathcal{A}(U)| = \kappa$.
For Noetherian objects $M$ and $N$, there is an injection of sets
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(M, N) \hookrightarrow \{\text{subobjects of } M \oplus N\}, \qquad f \longmapsto \big[\begin{psmallmatrix}1\\f\end{psmallmatrix} : M \to M \oplus N\big].
\]
Since the collection of subobjects of $M \oplus N$ is bounded by $\kappa$, one has $|\mathrm{Hom}_\mathcal{A}(M, N)| \leq \kappa$.

We then show for each $n \in \mathbb N$ inductively the proposition $\mathfrak P(n)$:
\begin{quote}
  $B_n$ is a quotient of a coproduct of at most $\kappa$ objects $U_i$, and $|\Omega_n|\leq\kappa$.
\end{quote}
Since $B_0$ is Noetherian, it is a quotient of a finite coproduct of the $U_i$; the preceding estimates give $|\Omega_0|\leq\kappa$, so $\mathfrak P(0)$ holds.
Suppose $\mathfrak P(n)$ holds for some $n \in \mathbb N$.
By construction $B_{n+1}$ is a quotient of $B_n\oplus\coprod_{(i,S,f)\in\Omega_n}U_i$.
Since $|\Omega_n|\leq\kappa$, it is again a quotient of a coproduct of at most $\kappa$ objects $U_i$.
The preceding estimates bound the number of pairs $(i,S)$ and the size of each $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(S,B_{n+1})$ by $\kappa$, so $|\Omega_{n+1}|\leq\kappa$.
This yields $\mathfrak P(n+1)$, and the claim follows by induction.

Since $E=\bigcup_{n<\omega}B_n$, it is a quotient of $\coprod_{n<\omega}B_n$.
Combining the epimorphisms onto the $B_n$ and using that $\kappa$ is infinite gives the required quotient of at most $\kappa$ objects $U_i$.
This completes the proof.

label: lem:small-injectives
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{lem:small-injectives}
  For a set of objects $(Y_t)_{t \in T}\subseteq \mathcal A$, every map from an indecomposable injective object $E$ to $\coprod_{t\in T}Y_t$ factors through some $\coprod_{t \in T'} Y_{t}$, where $T' \subseteq T$ and $|T'| \leq \kappa$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:card-criterion}, $E$ is a quotient of $\coprod_{s \in S} U_s$ where each $U_s$ is a Noetherian subobject of $U$ and $|S| \leq \kappa$.
  Then consider the composition $g : \coprod_{s \in S} U_s \twoheadrightarrow E \to \coprod_{t\in T}Y_t$.
  For each $s \in S$, the restriction $g : U_s \to \coprod_{t\in T}Y_t$ factors through a finite subcoproduct $\coprod_{t \in T_s} Y_t$ with $T_s \subseteq T$ finite.
  Set $T'=\bigcup_{s\in S}T_s$; then $|T'|\leq\kappa$, and $g$ factors through $\coprod_{t\in T'}Y_t$.
  The projection to $\coprod_{t\in T\setminus T'}Y_t$ vanishes after the quotient epimorphism, hence vanishes on $E$.
  Thus the original map factors through the same subcoproduct.

label: prop:cardinal-criterion
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:cardinal-criterion}
  The class $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under arbitrary coproducts if it is closed under $\kappa$-indexed coproducts.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(G_i)_{i\in I}$ be Gorenstein injective objects, and choose complete injective resolutions $T_i$ with $Z^0T_i\cong G_i$.
Then $T=\coprod_{i\in I}T_i$ is acyclic with injective terms and $Z^nT=\coprod_{i\in I}Z^nT_i$.
To see that $T$ is totally acyclic, it suffices to show that $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,T)$ is acyclic for each indecomposable injective object $E$: this follows from the canonical isomorphism $\prod_{i} \mathrm{Ext}^1_\mathcal{A}(X_i, Y) \cong \mathrm{Ext}^1_\mathcal{A}(\coprod_{i}X_i, Y)$ for Grothendieck categories.

For $E\in\mathcal E$, every map $f : E\to Z^nT$ factors, by Corollary~\ref{lem:small-injectives}, through $\coprod_{j\in J}Z^nT_j$ for some $J\subseteq I$ with $|J|\leq\kappa$.  
Put the restriction $f' : E\to \coprod_{j \in J}Z^n T_j$.
The exact sequence
\[
 0\longrightarrow\coprod_{j\in J}Z^{n-1}T_j\longrightarrow\coprod_{j\in J}T_j^{n-1}
 \longrightarrow\coprod_{j\in J}Z^nT_j\longrightarrow0
\]
has Gorenstein injective left term, so $f'$ lifts to $\coprod_{j \in J}T_j^{n-1}$, and hence $f$ lifts to $T^{n-1}$.
Thus $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,T)$ is acyclic.
It follows that $T$ is totally acyclic, and hence $Z^0T\cong\coprod_{i\in I}G_i$ is Gorenstein injective.

label: lem:tac-smallness
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:tac-smallness}
Every indecomposable injective object $E$ is $\kappa^+$-presentable.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first make explicit the cardinal estimates used below.
A Noetherian subobject of $U^{\oplus r}$ is the sum of the images of finitely many maps $U\to U^{\oplus r}$, so there are at most $\kappa$ such subobjects.
Every Noetherian object $M$ is a quotient of a Noetherian subobject $L\subseteq U^{\oplus r}$: choose an epimorphism $U^{\oplus r}\twoheadrightarrow M$ and use the directed union of Noetherian subobjects of its source to find $L$ mapping onto $M$.
Preimages in $L$ therefore bound the subobjects of $M$ by $\kappa$.
Graphs in $M\oplus N$ then give $|\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,N)|\leq\kappa$ for Noetherian $M,N$.
By Proposition~\ref{prop:card-criterion}, $E$ is a quotient of a coproduct of at most $\kappa$ Noetherian objects.
The images of the finite subcoproducts form a directed family of at most $\kappa$ Noetherian subobjects with union $E$.
Noetherian objects in $\mathcal A$ are finitely presented, so this expresses $E$ as a $\kappa^+$-small colimit of $\kappa^+$-presentable objects.
Hence $E$ is $\kappa^+$-presentable, since $\kappa^+$-filtered colimits of sets commute with $\kappa^+$-small limits.
head: environment

label: cor:small-coproduct-presentable
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:small-coproduct-presentable}
A coproduct of $\leq 2^\kappa$ indecomposable injective objects is $\lambda$-presentable.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:tac-smallness}, each summand is $\lambda$-presentable.
Hom out of the coproduct is a product of fewer than $\lambda=(2^\kappa)^+$ Hom functors, and $\lambda$-filtered colimits of sets commute with such products.
head: environment

label: lem:small-coproduct-subobjects
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:small-coproduct-subobjects}
A coproduct of at most $2^\kappa$ indecomposable injective objects has at most $2^\kappa$ Noetherian subobjects.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:card-criterion}, every finite coproduct of indecomposable injectives is a directed union of at most $\kappa$ Noetherian subobjects, obtained as images of finite subcoproducts of a Noetherian presentation.
Each has at most $\kappa$ subobjects, and every Noetherian subobject of the union lies in one of them.
Thus a finite coproduct has at most $\kappa$ Noetherian subobjects.
For the asserted bound, every Noetherian subobject lies in a finite subcoproduct, and there are at most $2^\kappa$ finite subcoproducts.
head: environment

label: cor:small-coproduct-hom
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:small-coproduct-hom}
For every indecomposable injective object $E$ and every coproduct $X$ of at most $2^\kappa$ indecomposable injective objects, one has $|\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,X)|\leq2^\kappa$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For a Noetherian object $N$, every map $N\to X$ has Noetherian image.
There are at most $2^\kappa$ possible images by Lemma~\ref{lem:small-coproduct-subobjects}, and at most $\kappa$ maps to each by the Noetherian Hom estimate recalled above.
Choose an epimorphism $\coprod_{i\in I}U_i\twoheadrightarrow E$ as in Proposition~\ref{prop:card-criterion}, with $|I|\leq\kappa$ and each $U_i$ Noetherian.
Then
\[
 |\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,X)|
 \leq\prod_{i\in I}|\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(U_i,X)|
 \leq(2^\kappa)^\kappa=2^\kappa.
\]

label: prop:small-tac-subcomplex
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:small-tac-subcomplex}
The class $\mathcal C$ is $\lambda$-Kaplansky in $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The result is known when $\mathcal A$ is a module category; \cite[Lemma~4.1.9 and Remark~4.1.10]{EnochsJenda2011VolII}.
This lemma generalises the result to locally finitely generated Grothendieck category, where Noetherian subobjects replace finite sets of elements.

Fix $T \in \mathcal C$ and a $\lambda$-presentable subcomplex $Y\subseteq T$.
It is clear that each $Y^n$ is $\lambda$-presentable.
Then decompose $T^n=\coprod_{a\in A^n}E_{n,a}$ into indecomposable injectives.
It remains to construct a $\lambda$-presentable complex $V$ with $Y \subseteq V \subseteq T$ and $V, T/V \in \mathcal C$.
The construction is given by transfinite induction on a continuous $\kappa^+$-chain, which yields $Y \subseteq V_0 \subseteq V_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq V_\beta \subseteq V_{\beta + 1} \subseteq \cdots$ with $\bigcup_{\beta < \kappa^+} V_\beta = V$, and is supposed to satisfy
\[
 V_\beta^n=\coprod_{a\in A_\beta^n}E_{n,a},
 \qquad A_\beta^n\subseteq A^n,
 \qquad |A_\beta^n|\leq2^\kappa,
\]

We first construct $V_0$ by induction.
Since the subcoproducts of $T^n$ with $\leq 2^\kappa$ summands form a $\lambda$-filtered union and $Y^n$ is $\lambda$-presentable, the inclusion $Y^n \subseteq T^n$ passes through some subcoproduct $\coprod_{a \in {}^{(0)}A^{n}_0}E_{n,a}$, denoted by ${}^{(0)}V_0^n$.
Note that $d({}^{(0)}V_0^{n})$ is not necessarily contained in ${}^{(0)}V_0^{n+1}$.
Hence we take the refinement ${}^{(1)}V_0^{n+1} = \coprod_{a \in {}^{(1)}A^{n+1}_0}E_{n+1,a}$ so that ${}^{(0)}V_0^{n+1} + d({}^{(0)}V_0^{n}) \subseteq {}^{(1)}V_0^{n+1}$.
By Corollary~\ref{lem:small-injectives}, the differential of each indecomposable summand factors through $\leq \kappa$ summands in the next degree.
Hence ${}^{(0)}V_0^{n+1} + d({}^{(0)}V_0^{n})$ factors through $\leq 2^\kappa + 2^\kappa \cdot \kappa = 2^\kappa$ summands and thus we may assume $|{}^{(1)}A_0^{n+1}| \leq 2^\kappa$.
By induction, one obtains
\[
\xymatrix@C=1cm@R=0.5cm{
\vdots \ar[dr]
& \vdots \ar[dr]
& \vdots
&
& \vdots \ar[d]
\\
{}^{(0)}V_0^{n-1} \ar@{}[r]|{\subset} \ar[dr]
& {}^{(1)}V_0^{n-1} \ar@{}[r]|{\subset} \ar[dr]
& {}^{(2)}V_0^{n-1} \ar@{}[r]|{\subset}
& \cdots
& V_0^{n-1} \ar[d]
\\
{}^{(0)}V_0^n \ar@{}[r]|{\subset} \ar[dr]
& {}^{(1)}V_0^n \ar@{}[r]|{\subset} \ar[dr]
& {}^{(2)}V_0^n \ar@{}[r]|{\subset}
& \cdots
& V_0^n \ar[d]
\\
{}^{(0)}V_0^{n+1} \ar@{}[r]|{\subset} \ar[dr]
& {}^{(1)}V_0^{n+1} \ar@{}[r]|{\subset} \ar[dr]
& {}^{(2)}V_0^{n+1} \ar@{}[r]|{\subset}
& \cdots
& V_0^{n+1} \ar[d]
\\
\vdots & \vdots & \vdots && \vdots
}
\]
Here ${}^{(m)}V_0^n = \coprod_{a \in {}^{(m)}A_0^n}E_{n,a}$, $|{}^{(m)}A_0^n| \leq 2^\kappa$ and ${}^{(m)}V_0^n+d_T^{n-1}({}^{(m)}V_0^{n-1})\subseteq{}^{(m+1)}V_0^n$.
Each solid arrow denote the differential restricted to subobjects.
Taking $V_0^n = \bigcup_{m \in \mathbb N}{}^{(m)}V_0^n$ completes the construction of $V_0$.

Suppose now that $V_\beta$ is constructed for some $\beta < \kappa^+$, then we construct $V_{\beta + 1}$.
Consider $Z^n V_\beta \subseteq V_\beta^n$.
For each Noetherian subobject $N \subseteq Z^n V_\beta$, one can take another noetherian object $N' \subseteq T^{n-1}$ such that the restricted $d : N' \to N$ is epic: indeed $N \subseteq Z^n T = B^n T$, and the preimage of $N$ along $d$ is a filtered union of its Noetherian subobjects.
Each such $N' \subseteq T^{n-1}$ lies in a finite subcoproduct indexed by $S_\beta^{n-1}(N')$, and one fixes the correspondence $N \mapsto S_\beta^{n-1}(N')$.
For each morphism $f$ from indecomposable injective $E$ to $Z^n T$, fix a lifting $\widetilde f : E \to T^{n-1}$.
By Corollary~\ref{lem:small-injectives}, $\widetilde f$ factors through a subcoproduct indexed by a set $L_\beta^{n-1}(\widetilde f)\subseteq A^{n-1}$ with $|L_\beta^{n-1}(\widetilde f)|\leq\kappa$.
Fix such $L_\beta^{n-1}(\widetilde f)$ for each $f$.
Take
\[
{}^{(0)}A_{\beta+1}^{n-1} = A_{\beta}^{n-1} \cup \bigcup_{N \subseteq Z^n V_\beta \ \text{Noetherian}} S_\beta^{n-1}(N') \cup \bigcup_{\substack{f : E \to Z^n V_\beta\\ E \ \text{indecomposable injective}}}L_\beta^{n-1}(\widetilde f).
\]
By construction $|A_{\beta}^{n-1}| \leq 2^\kappa$.
Since $V^n_\beta$ is a coproduct of $\leq 2^\kappa$ indecomposable injective objects, $Z^n V_\beta$ has $\leq 2^\kappa$ Noetherian subobjects.
Hence $|\bigcup_{N \subseteq Z^n V_\beta \ \text{Noetherian}} S_\beta^{n-1}(N')| \leq 2^\kappa$.
Each indecomposable injective object is an injective envelope of some Noetherian object, thus they has cardinal $\leq \kappa$.
By Corollary~\ref{cor:small-coproduct-hom}, $|\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E, Z^n V_\beta)|\leq 2^\kappa$.
It follows that $|{}^{(0)}A_{\beta+1}^{n-1}| \leq 2^\kappa$.
By the same construction in the initial setup, one obtains ${}^{(m)}A_{\beta+1}^{n}$ for each $n \in \mathbb Z$ and $m \in \mathbb N$.
Taking $A_{\beta + 1}^n = \bigcup_{m \in \mathbb N} {}^{(m)} A_{\beta+1}^n$ completes the construction of $V_{\beta+1}$.

Suppose that for any limit ordinal $\delta \leq \kappa^+$, each $(V_\beta)_{\beta < \delta}$ is constructed.
Take $V_\delta = \bigcup_{\beta < \delta} V_\beta$.
By construction $V_\delta ^n = \coprod_{a \in A_{\beta+1} ^n} E_{n,a}$, where $A_{\beta+1}^n =\bigcup _{\beta < \delta} A_\beta ^n$ has cardinal $\leq 2^\kappa$.
We claim that $V_\delta$ is an exact complex.
On one hand, $V_\beta$ is a complex since each Noetherian subobject $N \subseteq V_\delta^n$ lies in some $V_\alpha^n$ for $\alpha < \delta$, thus $N$ is annihilated by $d^2$.
On the other hand, each Noetherian subobject $N \subseteq Z^n V_\delta$ lies in $Z^n V_\beta$ for some $\beta < \delta$, and thus lies in $B^n V_{\beta+1}$ by construction.

Take $V=V_{\kappa^+}$.
By construction, $V$ is an acyclic complex with injective terms, and each $V^n$ is $\lambda$-presentable by Corollary~\ref{cor:small-coproduct-presentable}.
The equaliser description of chain maps uses only countable products of degreewise Hom sets, which commute with $\lambda$-filtered colimits; hence $V$ is $\lambda$-presentable in $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)$.
To see that $V\in\mathcal C$, it remains to show that every map $f:E\to Z^{n+1}V$, with $E$ indecomposable injective, lifts to $V^n$.
By Corollary~\ref{lem:small-injectives}, the composite $E\to Z^{n+1}V\hookrightarrow V^{n+1}$ factors through a subcoproduct with at most $\kappa$ summands.
Since $\kappa^+$ is regular, all these summands lie in some $V_\beta^{n+1}$ with $\beta<\kappa^+$.
Thus $f$ factors through $Z^{n+1}V_\beta$ and, by the successor construction, lifts to $V_{\beta+1}^n\subseteq V^n$.
Hence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,V)$ is acyclic for every indecomposable injective $E$.
Every injective object is a coproduct of indecomposable injectives, and products of exact complexes of abelian groups are exact; therefore $V\in\mathcal C$.

Each $V^n$ is a subcoproduct of $T^n$, so $0\to V\to T\to T/V\to 0$ is degreewise split and $T/V$ has injective terms.
Since $V$ and $T$ are acyclic, so is $T/V$.
For every injective object $E$, applying $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,-)$ gives a short exact sequence of complexes of abelian groups.
Hence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(E,T/V)$ is acyclic.
Thus $T/V\in\mathcal C$.

We have constructed a $\lambda$-presentable subcomplex $V$ with $Y\subseteq V\subseteq T$ and $V,T/V\in\mathcal C$.
Hence $\mathcal C$ is $\lambda$-Kaplansky.

title: Proposition

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:small-tac-subcomplex}, the class $\mathcal C$ is Kaplansky, and it is clearly extension-closed.
By the assumption that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under filtered colimits and the exactness of filtered colimits, $\mathcal C$ is closed under filtered colimits.
By \cite[Proposition~1.6]{CEI2017}, an extension-closed Kaplansky class closed under filtered colimits in a Grothendieck category is covering.
Applying this result in $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)$ proves the assertion.

title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathcal C$ denote the class of totally acyclic complexes of injective objects.
The functor $Z^0:\mathcal C\to\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is essentially surjective and full and there are natural isomorphisms
\[
\Phi : \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)}(T,M[1])
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z^0T,M)
\qquad(T\in\mathcal C).
\]
Here $M$ is the stalk complex concentrated in degree $0$.
It is straightforward to show that a $\mathcal C$-(pre)cover $\tau:T\to M[1]$, yields a $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$-(pre)cover $\Phi(\tau):Z^0T\to M$.
Hence $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is covering whenever $\mathcal C$ is covering.

title: Proof

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:noetherian-reduction}, each of the conditions implies that $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian.
We therefore assume throughout that $\mathcal A$ is locally Noetherian.
The proof is organised as follows:
\[
\xymatrix@C=2cm@R=.5cm{
(4) \ar@{->}[r] & (2) \ar@{->}[r] & (6) \ar@{->}[d]_{\square} \ar@<-0.6ex>@{->}[r] & (7) \ar@<-0.6ex>@{->}[l]_{\star} \\
(3) \ar@{->}[u] & (1) \ar@{->}[l] & (5) \ar@{->}[l]_{\triangle} \ar@{->}[r] & (8) \ar@{->}[lu]
}.
\]

\noindent\textit{$(1)\implies (3) \implies (4) \implies (2)$.}
By Wakamatsu lemma \cite[Lemma~7.1.13\textup{(1)}]{Krause2022}, An extension-closed covering class is special covering.
Hence $(1)$ implies $(3)$.
The implications $(3) \implies (4) \implies (2)$ are clear.

\noindent\textit{$(2)\implies (6)$.}
Suppose that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is a precovering class.
Let $(G_i)_{i \in I}$ be a collection of Gorenstein injective objects.
By assumption, there is a $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$-precover $G \to \coprod_{i \in I} G_i$.
Since each structure map $G_i \to \coprod_{i \in I} G_i$ lifts to $G_i \to G$, $\coprod_{i \in I}G$ is a summand of $G$.
Hence $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under coproducts, and $(2) \implies (6)$ follows.

\noindent\textit{$(5)\Longrightarrow(1)$.}
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:gi-covering-from-colimits}.

\noindent\textit{$(6)\Longrightarrow(5)$.}
Assume that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ is closed under coproducts.
Let $\mathcal C$ be the class of totally acyclic complexes of injective terms.
Then $\mathcal C$ is closed under coproducts, and thus $K_{\mathrm{tac}}(\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A) \subseteq K(\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A)$ is localising.
For a filtered diagram $(G_d)_{d \in D}$, the functorial construction of complete injective resolution Proposition~\ref{lem:gi-basic} yields a diagram $\mathbf I(G_d)$.
Then by Corollary~\ref{cor:localizing-colimit}, the degreewise colimit $\varinjlim_{d \in D} \mathbf I (G_d)$ is totally acyclic.
Exactness of filtered colimits gives $\varinjlim_dG_d\cong Z^0\!\left(\varinjlim_d\mathbf I(G_d)\right)$, proving \textup{(5)}.


\noindent\textit{$(6)\Longleftrightarrow(7)$.}
We only prove $(7) \implies (6)$.
If $\mathrm{End}_{\mathcal A}(U)$ is finite, Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-endomorphism-generator} gives \textup{(1)}, hence \textup{(6)} and \textup{(7)};
otherwise apply Proposition~\ref{prop:cardinal-criterion}.

\noindent\textit{$(5)\Longrightarrow(8)$.}
Put $\mathcal T=K(\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A)$ and $\mathcal S=K_{\mathrm{tac}}(\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A)$.
Since precover of chain complexes passes to its homotopy category, Proposition~\ref{lem:tac-approximations} gives right $\mathcal S$-approximations in $\mathcal T$.
Since $\mathcal T$ has countable coproducts and $\mathcal S$ is thick, both have split idempotents.
Thus the inclusion $i_\ast : \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal T$ of localising subcategory has a right adjoint by \cite[Proposition~3.2]{KrauseApproximations}.

\noindent\textit{$(8)\Longrightarrow(6)$.}
Suppose that $i_\ast:\mathcal S\to\mathcal T$ has right adjoint $i^!$.
For a family $(S_i)_{i \in I}$ in $\mathcal S$, put $S=\coprod_{i \in I} S_i$. Since $\mathcal{S}$ is a thick subcategory of $\mathcal{T}$, it follows from \cite[Lemma~3.2]{Krause2005} that the Verdier quotient functor $j^*:\mathcal{T}\longrightarrow \mathcal{T}/\mathcal{S}$ admits a right adjoint. Thus $j^*$ preserves coproducts, and hence $S\in \mathrm{Ker}(j^*)$. Since $\mathcal{S}$ is a thick subcategory of $\mathcal{T}$, $\mathrm{Ker}(j^*)=\mathcal{S}$ and hence $S\in \mathcal{S}$. Therefore $\mathcal{S}$ is closed under coproducts.

label: prop:leftadj
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The equivalence $(2)\Longleftrightarrow(3)$ follows from \cite[Corollary~5.8]{EG26}, since a generating set in ${}^\perp\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ can be replaced by its coproduct.

\noindent\textit{$(3)\Longrightarrow(1)$.}
Let $\mathcal C \subseteq \mathrm{Ch}(\mathrm{Inj}\mathcal A)$ be the collection of totally acyclic complexes.
By \cite[Corollary~4.3]{EG26}, every $T\in\mathcal T$ admits a special $\mathcal C$-preenvelope $e_T:T \to C_T$, which yields degreewise split short exact sequence in $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathcal A)$
\[
0\longrightarrow T\longrightarrow C_T\longrightarrow V_T\longrightarrow0, \qquad C_T \in \mathcal C, \quad V_T \in {}^\perp \mathcal C.
\]
This yields a distinguished triangle $T \xrightarrow{e_T}C_T \to V_T \to T[1]$ in $\mathcal T$.
For each $S \in \mathcal S$ and $n \in \mathbb Z$, the orthogonal relation yields that $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(V_T[n], S) = 0$.
Hence
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(C_T, S) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C_T, S) \xrightarrow[\sim]{- \circ e_T} \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(T, S).
\]
It follows that $T \mapsto C_T$ defines a left adjoint of $i_\ast$.

\noindent\textit{$(1)\Longrightarrow(3)$.}
Let $E$ be an injective resolution of a generator $U$.
Then complete the unit $\eta_E : E \to i_\ast i^\ast E$ to the distinguished triangle $E\xlongrightarrow{\eta_E} i_\ast i^\ast E\longrightarrow C\longrightarrow E[1]$.
For each $S \in \mathcal S$, adjunction $i^\ast \dashv i_\ast$ gives $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(\eta_E, S) : \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(i_\ast i^\ast E, S) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(E, S)$.
Hence $\mathrm{Cone}(\eta_E)\in{}^\perp\mathcal S$.
Since $i_\ast i^\ast E$ is acyclic, $H^{-1}C\longrightarrow H^0E\cong U$.
Since $U$ is a quotient of $Z^{-1} C$, one sees that $Z^{-1}C$ is a generator.
Since $H^{>0}(C[-1])=0$, \cite[Lemma~7.1]{Krause2005} gives
\[
\overline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,Z^0S)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(C[-1],S)=0
\qquad(S\in\mathcal S),
\]
where $\overline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(-,?) = \frac{{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(-,?)}{\{\text{morphisms factors through injectives}\}}$.
Apply $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,-)$ to
\[
0\longrightarrow Z^{-1}S\longrightarrow S^{-1}
\xlongrightarrow \pi Z^0S\longrightarrow0.
\]
Since $S^{-1}$ is injective, this gives
\[
\mathrm{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,Z^{-1}S)
\cong
\frac{\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,Z^0S)}
{\mathrm{Im}\ \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,\pi)}.
\]
By total acyclicity, every map from an injective object to $Z^0S$ passes through $S^{-1}\to Z^0S$.
Thus $\mathrm{Im}\ \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,\pi)$ consists precisely of the maps in $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,Z^0S)$ factoring through injective objects.
Hence
\[
\mathrm{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,Z^{-1}S)
\cong\overline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathcal A}(Z^{-1}C,Z^0S)=0.
\]
Every object in $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$ occurs as $Z^{-1}S$ for some $S\in\mathcal S$.
Thus $Z^{-1}C\in{}^\perp\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A)$.

title: Remark
body_md:
If $i_\ast$ has a left adjoint, then $\mathcal S$ has arbitrary coproducts
    \[
    \coprod_{i \in I} ^{\mathcal S} S_i \cong i^\ast \left(\coprod_{i \in I}^{\mathcal T} i_\ast (S_i)\right).

label: prop:tac-recollement
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:tac-recollement}
The inclusion $i_\ast$ has both adjoints if and only if
\[
\mathcal S\xrightarrow{i_\ast}\mathcal T
\xrightarrow{j^\ast}\mathcal Q:=\mathcal T/\mathcal S
\]
extends to a recollement.
In this case, $\mathcal Q$ is locally small, and
\[
i^\ast\dashv i_\ast\dashv i^!,\qquad
j_!\dashv j^\ast\dashv j_\ast,\qquad
{}^\perp\mathcal S\simeq\mathcal Q\simeq\mathcal S^\perp,
\]
where $j_!$ and $j_\ast$ identify $\mathcal Q$ with ${}^\perp\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal S^\perp$, respectively.

title: Proof
body_md: Apply \cite[Lemma~3.2]{Krause2005} and its dual to the thick subcategory $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal T$.

title: Example
body_md:
Let $R$ be a ring such that $\mathcal{GI}(R)$ forms a covering class.
Put $\mathcal S = K_{\mathrm{tac}}(\mathrm{Inj}\,R)$ and $\mathcal T = K(\mathrm{Inj}\,R)$, respectively.
Then one has the adjoint triple
\[
\xymatrix@C=3cm{
\mathcal S
\ar@{ >->}[r]|{i_\ast}
& \mathcal T
\ar@<1.2ex>[l]^{i^!}
\ar@<-1.2ex>[l]_{i^\ast}
}
\]
where $i_\ast:\mathcal S\to\mathcal T$ is the canonical inclusion.

Let $\mathcal M$ be a set of representatives of the finitely generated objects of $\mathrm{Mod}_R$, and choose an injective resolution $\iota M$ for each $M\in\mathcal M$.
Then the objects $i^\ast(\iota M)$, $M\in\mathcal M$, form a set of compact generators of $\mathcal S$, and the compact objects of $\mathcal S$ are
\[
 \mathcal S^c=\operatorname{thick}_{\mathcal S}\{i^\ast(\iota M) \mid M\in\mathcal M\}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence}, $R$ is Noetherian and $\mathcal S$ is localising in $\mathcal T$.
The category $\mathcal T$ is compactly generated by the $\iota M$ \cite[Proposition~2.3]{Krause2005}.
The left adjoint $i^\ast$ exists taking $U = R$ in Lemma~\ref{prop:leftadj} (3).
The inclusion $i_\ast:\mathcal S\to\mathcal T$ preserves coproducts.
By adjunction
\[
 \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(i^\ast(\iota M),-)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(\iota M,i_\ast(-)),
\]
every $i^\ast(\iota M)$ is compact.
If $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal S}(i^\ast(\iota M),X[n])=0$ for every $M\in\mathcal M$ and $n\in\mathbb Z$, adjunction gives $i_\ast X=0$, hence $X=0$.
Thus these objects generate $\mathcal S$, and its compact objects are their thick closure \cite[Proposition~3.4.15]{Krause2022}.

label: lem:A-local
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:A-local}
$A$ is a local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap t\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]=(t,s_1,s_2)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It is straightforward to check that $A$ is a ring. 
Since $A\subseteq F$, $A$ is a domain. 

We claim that $\mathfrak m_A=A\cap t\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ is the unique maximal ideal.
It suffices to show that each $a \in A \setminus \mathfrak m_A$ is a unit.
Note that $a$ is a unit in $F \cap \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$.
It remains to show that $a^{-1} \in A$.
By construction, $\delta_i(a^{-1}) = -a^{-2}\delta _i (a) \in \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ for $i = 1,2$.
Thus $a^{-1} \in A$, proving the claim.

We next prove that $\mathfrak m_A=(t,s_1,s_2)$. 
Clearly $(t,s_1,s_2)\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. 
Conversely, fix an arbitrary $b\in\mathfrak m_A$.
For each $i =1 ,2$, $b$ takes the form $\delta_i(b)=c_i+td_i$ with $c_i \in \mathbb Q$ and $d_i \in \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$.
Set $c=b-c_1s_1-c_2s_2$.
Then $c\in t\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ and hence $c/t\in F\cap \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$. 
Since for each $i = 1,2$, \(
\delta_i(c/t)=\frac{\delta_i(c)}{t}=\frac{\delta_i(b)-c_i}{t}=d_i\in \mathbb Q[\![t]\!].\) By definition $c / t \in A$, and hence $c\in tA$. 
It follows that $b\in At+As_1+As_2$, proving $\mathfrak m_A \subseteq (t,s_1,s_2)$. 
This completes the proof.
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md: For the local domain $(A, \mathfrak m_A)$, one has $\mathfrak m_A^2=t\mathfrak m_A$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
On one hand, any $b,c\in\mathfrak m_A$ yield that $bc/t\in t\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$. 
Since \(\delta_i(bc/t)=\frac{b\delta_i(c)+c\delta_i(b)}{t}\in \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\), $bc/t\in\mathfrak m_A$. 
Thus \(\mathfrak m_A^2\subseteq t\mathfrak m_A\). 
On the other hand, $\mathfrak m_A^2 \supseteq t\mathfrak m_A$ follows from $t\in\mathfrak m_A$.

label: lem:A-noeth
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{lem:A-noeth}
For every $a\in A \setminus \{0\}$, $A/(a)$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-vector space.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $a$ is a unit, there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, let $r\in\mathbb N$ be the largest integer such that $a\in t^r\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$. Then $r\geq1$.
Then $t^{2r}/a\in F\cap \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$, and
\[
\delta_i(t^{2r}/a)=-\frac{t^{2r}\delta_i(a)}{a^2}\in \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]
\qquad(i=1,2).
\]
Thus $t^{2r}/a\in A$.
It follows that $t^{2r}\in aA$, and $\mathfrak m_A^{2r+1}=t^{2r}\mathfrak m_A\subseteq aA$.
Since $\mathfrak m_A=(t,s_1,s_2)$ is finitely generated with residue field $A/\mathfrak m_A\cong\mathbb Q$,
each $\mathfrak m_A^k/\mathfrak m_A^{k+1}$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$.
Hence $A/\mathfrak m_A^{2r+1}$, and therefore its quotient $A/aA$, is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$.
head: environment

label: cor:A-noetherian
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:A-noetherian}
    $A$ is Noetherian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $0\ne I\subseteq A$ be an ideal and choose $0\ne a\in I$.
By Proposition~\ref{lem:A-noeth}, $I/aA$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$.
Lifting a basis gives $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in I$ with $I=(a,b_1,\ldots,b_r)$.
Thus every ideal of $A$ is finitely generated.

label: lem:dimA
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $0\ne\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec} A$ and choose $0\ne a\in\mathfrak q$.
Then $A/\mathfrak q$ is a domain and a quotient of the finite-dimensional
$\mathbb Q$-algebra $A/aA$. Hence $A/\mathfrak q$ is a field, so
$\mathfrak q$ is maximal. Since $A$ is local, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_A$.
As $t$ is a nonzero nonunit, \((0)\subsetneq\mathfrak m_A\),
and therefore $\dim A=1$.

label: lem:R
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:R}
$R$ is a commutative Cohen--Macaulay local ring of Krull dimension one.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $R$ is a finitely generated $A$-algebra, $R$ is Noetherian.
Consider the ring surjection with the nilpotent kernel
\[
R \longrightarrow A, \qquad \begin{psmallmatrix}
a&b&c\\
0&a&0\\
0&0&a
\end{psmallmatrix} \longmapsto a.
\]
Hence $\operatorname{Spec}A = \mathrm{Spec} R$.
Thus $R$ is local with Krull dimension $1$.

Since multiplying by $t$ is injective on $R$, one has $\operatorname{depth}R\ge1$.
On the other hand \(\operatorname{depth}R \le \dim R=1\).
Hence $R$ is Cohen--Macaulay.
head: environment

label: lem:A-localisation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:A-localisation}
One has $A[t^{-1}]=F$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inclusion $A[t^{-1}]\subseteq F$ is clear. Conversely, let $f\in F$.
Choose $N$ sufficiently large that \(t^Nf, t^N\delta_1(f), t^N\delta_2(f)\)
all lie in $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$. Since $\delta_i(t)=0$,
\(\delta_i(t^Nf)=t^N\delta_i(f)\in \mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\).
Thus $t^Nf\in A$, and hence $f\in A[t^{-1}]$.
head: environment

label: lem:J-injective
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:J-injective}
    $E_{R[t^{-1}]}(F) \cong E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$ as $R$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $R/\mathfrak n\subseteq E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$ is an essential extension of $R$-modules, and multiplying by $t$ is injective on $R / \mathfrak n \cong A$, one sees that multiplying by $t$ is injective on $E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$.
Since $E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$ is and indecomposable injective module, $t : E_R(R/\mathfrak n) \to E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$ is an automorphism.
By \cite[Lemma~3.2.5]{BrunsHerzog}, injective envelope is compatible with localisations, which gives
\[
E_R(R/\mathfrak n)\cong E_R(R/\mathfrak n)[t^{-1}]\cong E_{R[t^{-1}]}((R/\mathfrak n)[t^{-1}])=E_{R[t^{-1}]}(F).
\]
This completes the proof.

label: prop:finite-local-injective
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:finite-local-injective}
Let $(B,\mathfrak p)\to(T,\mathfrak m)$ be a homomorphism of commutative Noetherian local rings.
Suppose that $T$ is a finitely generated $B$-module, and the morphism induces an isomorphism of residue fields $k = B/ \mathfrak p \cong T/\mathfrak m$.
Then $E_T(k)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_B(T,E_B(k))$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cite[Lemma~3.1.6]{BrunsHerzog}, $\mathrm{Hom}_B(T,E_B(k))$ is injective over $T$, and adjunction gives
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_T(k,\mathrm{Hom}_B(T,E_B(k)))\cong\mathrm{Hom}_B(k,E_B(k))\cong k.
\]
The module $E_B(k)$ is $\mathfrak p$-torsion, i.e., every element is
annihilated by some power of $\mathfrak p$ \cite[Theorem~18.4(v)]{Matsumura1989}.
Since $T$ is a finitely generated $B$-module, $\mathrm{Hom}_B(T,E_B(k))$ is also $\mathfrak p$-torsion.
Moreover, $T/\mathfrak pT$ is an Artinian local ring, so $\mathfrak m^h\subseteq\mathfrak pT$ for some $h$.
Hence $\mathrm{Hom}_B(T,E_B(k))$ is $\mathfrak m$-torsion with one-dimensional socle $k$.
In this case $k$ is essential, and thus $E_T(k) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_B(T,E_B(k))$.
This completes the proof.
head: environment

label: cor:J-Hom
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:J-Hom}
    $E_R(R/\mathfrak n) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_A(R,F)$ as $R$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-local-injective}, $F\to R[t^{-1}]$ yields
    \[
    E_R(R/\mathfrak n)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_F(R[t^{-1}],F)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_A(R,F).
    \]

title: Lemma
body_md: $\widehat A \cong \mathbb Q[\![t]\!] \otimes _{\mathbb Q} \mathbb Q[x_1, x_2]/(x_1,x_2)^2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first claim that the homomorphism
\[
A\longrightarrow \mathbb Q[\![t]\!][x_1, x_2]/(x_1, x_2)^2, \qquad 
a\longmapsto a+\delta_1(a)x_1+\delta_2(a)x_2
\]
induces, for each $q\ge1$, an isomorphism $A/t^qA\cong (\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/t^q\mathbb Q[\![t]\!])[x_1,x_2]/(x_1,x_2)^2$.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item It is injective. 
    If $a,\delta_1(a),\delta_2(a)\in t^q\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$, then $a \in t^qA$.
    \item It is surjective. 
    For $i=1,2$, choose $p_{i,q}\in\mathbb Q[t]$ with $s_i-p_{i,q}\in t^q\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$.
    Since $\delta_j(t)=0$ and $\delta_j(s_i-p_{i,q})=\delta_{ij}$, the map sends $t$ to $\bar t$ and $s_i-p_{i,q}$ to $x_i$.
    Note that $\bar t,x_1,x_2$ generate $(\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/t^q\mathbb Q[\![t]\!])[x_1,x_2]/(x_1,x_2)^2$ as a $\mathbb Q$-algebra,
    thus the induced map is surjective.
\end{enumerate}

Finally, $(t)$-adic and $\mathfrak m_A$-adic topologies are equivalent, since
\[
\mathfrak m_A^{q+1}=t^q\mathfrak m_A
\subseteq t^qA\subseteq\mathfrak m_A^q.
\]
Taking inverse limits gives 
\[
\widehat A
\cong \varprojlim_{q \geq 1} A/t^qA
\cong \varprojlim_{q \geq 1} (\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/t^q \mathbb Q[\![t]\!])[x_1, x_2]/(x_1,x_2)^2 \cong \mathbb Q[\![t]\!] \otimes \mathbb Q[x_1,x_2] / (x_1,x_2)^2.
\]
This completes the proof.

label: lem:E-injective
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:E-injective}
There is an isomorphism of $R$-modules
\[
E_R(\mathbb Q)\cong \bigl(\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]/\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\bigr)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}
\bigl(\mathbb Q[x_1,x_2]/(x_1,x_2)^2\bigr)^*
\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(\mathbb Q[u,v]/(u,v)^2\bigr)^*.
\]
Here $(-)^*=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(-,\mathbb Q)$, with the action on each dual factor given by $(af)(b)=f(ab)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ is a discrete valuation ring, $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]/\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ is injective over $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$, and its socle $t^{-1}\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\cong\mathbb Q$ is essential.
Thus $E_{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}(\mathbb Q)\cong \mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]/\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$.
The preceding completion formula shows that $\widehat R$ is a free $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$-module of rank $9$.
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-local-injective} to $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!] \to \widehat {R}$
therefore gives
\[
E_{\widehat R}(\mathbb Q)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}\bigl(\widehat R,\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]/\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\bigr).
\]
Finally, $E_R(\mathbb Q)\cong E_{\widehat R}(\mathbb Q)$ as $R$-modules by \cite[Theorem~18.6(iii)]{Matsumura1989}.
Since both polynomial quotient factors are finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$, tensor--Hom adjunction gives
\begin{align*}
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}\!\left(
\widehat R,\frac{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]}{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}\right)
&\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}\!\left(
\frac{\mathbb Q[x_1,x_2]}{(x_1,x_2)^2}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}
\frac{\mathbb Q[u,v]}{(u,v)^2},
\frac{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]}{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}\right)\\
&\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}\!\left(
\frac{\mathbb Q[x_1,x_2]}{(x_1,x_2)^2},
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}\!\left(
\frac{\mathbb Q[u,v]}{(u,v)^2},
\frac{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]}{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}\right)\right)\\
&\cong
\frac{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!][t^{-1}]}{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}
\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\left(\frac{\mathbb Q[x_1,x_2]}{(x_1,x_2)^2}\right)^*
\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\left(\frac{\mathbb Q[u,v]}{(u,v)^2}\right)^*.
\end{align*}

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:C-base-change}
For $C=\mathrm{Hom}_A(R,A)$, there are natural isomorphisms
\[
C\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*,\qquad
\widehat R\otimes_R C
\cong\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\otimes_{\mathbb Q}X\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*.

In particular, $C$ is finitely generated over $R$.

title: Proof

label: lem:E-tensor
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:E-tensor}
Both $P$ and $E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R} P$ are acyclic complexes.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $P$, define a $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!] \otimes X$-homomorphism $g : N \longrightarrow N$ (not an $\widehat R$-homomorphism)  via
\[ 
    e_{r,s} \longmapsto 0, \qquad ue_{r,s} \longmapsto e_{2r, s}, \qquad
    ve_{r,s} \longmapsto e_{2r+1,s}.
\]
Then $$\begin{psmallmatrix}g&0\\0&-g\end{psmallmatrix} \cdot \begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{psmallmatrix} + 
\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{psmallmatrix} \cdot \begin{psmallmatrix}g&0\\0&-g\end{psmallmatrix} = 1_P.$$
It follows that $1_P$ is setwise homotopic to zero, and thus $P$ is acyclic by \cite{BianZhangZhang2009}.

Write $E_R(\mathbb Q)=X^*\otimes_{\mathbb Q}V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*$, and let $\eta_0,\eta_1,\eta_2$ be dual to $1,x_1,x_2$.
We identify
\[
E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}N
\cong\coprod_{r,s\geq0}(X^*\otimes_{\mathbb Q}V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*)e_{r,s},
\]
and use $a,b,d$ also for the induced maps.
Define the $\mathbb Q$-linear map $k: E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}N
\longrightarrow E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}N$
via
\[
\begin{aligned}
(\eta_0\otimes w)e_{r,2s}
&\longmapsto (\eta_1\otimes w)e_{r,s},\\
(\eta_0\otimes w)e_{r,2s+1}
&\longmapsto (\eta_2\otimes w)e_{r,s},\\
(\eta_i\otimes w)e_{r,s}
&\longmapsto 0 \qquad (i=1,2),
\end{aligned}
\]
for $r,s\ge0$ and $w\in V\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*$.
Then
\[
\begin{psmallmatrix}0&k\\k&0\end{psmallmatrix}
\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{psmallmatrix}
+
\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{psmallmatrix}
\begin{psmallmatrix}0&k\\k&0\end{psmallmatrix}
=
1_{\left(E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}N\right)^{\oplus2}}.
\]
Thus $E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}P$ is acyclic
\cite{BianZhangZhang2009}.

label: prop:compGI
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:compGI}
    For each $n \in \mathbb N$, $\mathbf I \langle n\rangle$ is a totally acyclic complex with injective terms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Each term of $\mathbf I\langle n\rangle$ is a product of copies of $E_R(\mathbb Q)$, hence an injective $R$-module.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:E-tensor}, $P$ and thus $\mathbf C\langle n\rangle$ are acyclic.
Since $E_R(\mathbb Q) \cong E_{\widehat R}(\mathbb Q)$ is an injective $\widehat R$-module, it follows that $\mathbf I\langle n\rangle$ is acyclic.

Then we show that $\mathbf I\langle n\rangle$ is totally acyclic.
For an injective $R$-module $L$, one has
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_R(L,\mathbf I\langle n\rangle)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\widehat R}
\bigl(L\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle,E_R(\mathbb Q)\bigr).
\]
It suffices to show that $L\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle$ is acyclic.
Here we need only consider $L=E_R(\mathbb Q)$ and $L=E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$.
For the former, $\widehat R\otimes_R E_R(\mathbb Q)\cong E_R(\mathbb Q)$ by \cite[proof of Theorem~18.6(iii)]{Matsumura1989}.
\begin{align*}
L\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle
\cong E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}\mathbf C\langle n\rangle
\cong\mathrm{Cone}\bigl(t^n:E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}P
\longrightarrow E_R(\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\widehat R}P\bigr),
\end{align*}
which is acyclic by Lemma~\ref{lem:E-tensor}.
For the latter, $L\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle$ is the cone of $t^n : E_R(R/\mathfrak n)\otimes_RP \to E_R(R/\mathfrak n)\otimes_RP$, which is contractible since $t$ is an automorphism of $E_R(R/\mathfrak n)$; see the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:J-injective}.

label: lem:Q-free
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Q-free}\label{lem:Q}
The homology $H_0(Q)$ is a nonzero free $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$-module.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:C-base-change}, for each $i\in\mathbb Z$,
\[
Q_i=C\otimes_RP_i
\cong\left(\coprod_{r,s\geq0}(C\otimes_R\widehat R)e_{r,s}\right)^{2}\cong\left(\coprod_{r,s\geq0}
(\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\otimes_{\mathbb Q}X\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*)e_{r,s}\right)^{2}.
\]
The differential matrices $\begin{psmallmatrix}a&b\\b&-a\end{psmallmatrix}$ of $Q$
have entries in $\{0,1,-1\}\subseteq\mathbb Q$.
Let $Q'$ be the complex of $\mathbb Q$-vector spaces with terms $Q'_i=\left(\coprod_{r,s\geq0}(X\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*)e_{r,s}\right)^{2}$ and the same differential matrices.
Then $Q\cong\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Q'$ as complexes of $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$-modules.
Since $\mathbb Q$ is a field, the functor $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\otimes_{\mathbb Q}-$ is exact and therefore commutes with homology.
Consequently,
\[
H_0(Q)\cong\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\otimes_{\mathbb Q}H_0(Q').
\]
A $\mathbb Q$-basis of $H_0(Q')$ indexed by $\Lambda$ gives $H_0(Q)\cong\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$.
Hence $H_0(Q)$ is free.

To see that $H_0(Q) \neq 0$, consider $z=\bigl((1\otimes x_2\otimes\epsilon_v)e_{0,0},0\bigr)\in Q_0$.
By construction $z$ is a cycle.
Define a $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$-linear functional
$\lambda:Q_0\to\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ on the displayed basis by
\[
( (1\otimes\xi\otimes\epsilon)e_{r,s},0)
\longmapsto
\begin{cases}
1,&\xi=x_2,\ \epsilon=\epsilon_v,\ r=s=0,\\
0,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\qquad 
(0,(1\otimes\xi\otimes\epsilon)e_{r,s})\longmapsto 0.
\]
Thus $\lambda$ reads exactly the coefficient of
$(1\otimes x_2\otimes\epsilon_v)e_{0,0}$ in the first component, and $\lambda(z)=1$.

Then we show that $\lambda$ vanishes on boundaries, write an element of $Q_1$ as
$(p,q)$, where $p=\sum_{r,s}p_{r,s}e_{r,s}$ and
$q=\sum_{r,s}q_{r,s}e_{r,s}$, with finitely many nonzero coefficients in
$\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]\otimes_{\mathbb Q}X\otimes_{\mathbb Q}Y^*$.
Then $d(p,q)=(ap+bq,bp-aq)$.
Only the coefficient at $e_{0,0}$ in $ap+bq$ contributes to $\lambda$.
By construction, this coefficient is $u p_{0,0}+v p_{1,0}+x_1q_{0,0}$.
Now $u \cdot Y^*+v \cdot Y^*=\mathbb Q\epsilon_0$, so the first two terms have zero
$\epsilon_v$-coefficient.
Also $x_1 \cdot X=\mathbb Qx_1$, so the last term has zero $x_2$-coefficient.
Consequently,
\[
\lambda d(p,q)=0\quad\text{for every }(p,q)\in Q_1,
\qquad\lambda(z)=1.
\]
Hence $z\notin\mathrm{im}\,d_1$.
Since $z$ is a cycle, its class in $H_0(Q)$ is nonzero.

label: lem:Tn
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Tn}
For every $n\geq1$, one has $t^n\mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n)=0$ and $t^{n-1}\mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n)\ne0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The adjunction gives
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_R(C,\mathbf I\langle n\rangle)
=\mathrm{Hom}_R(C,\mathrm{Hom}_{\widehat R}( \mathbf C \langle n \rangle , E_R(\mathbb Q)))
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\widehat R}
\bigl(C\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle,E_R(\mathbb Q)\bigr).
\]
Since $C\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle
\cong\mathrm{Cone}(t^n:Q\to Q)$ taking homology groups of the distinguished triangle $Q \xrightarrow{t^n}Q \to C \otimes _R \mathbf C\langle n \rangle \to Q[1]$ gives a long exact sequence
\[
\cdots \longrightarrow H_{0}(Q) \xlongrightarrow{t^n} H_{0}(Q) \longrightarrow H_0(C \otimes _R \mathbf C\langle n \rangle) \longrightarrow H_{-1}(Q) \longrightarrow \cdots .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Q-free}, $t^n$ is injective on $H_i(Q)$.
Hence one has isomorphisms of $\widehat R$-modules
\[
H_i(C\otimes_R\mathbf C\langle n\rangle)
\cong H_0(Q)/t^nH_0(Q)\qquad(i\in\mathbb Z).
\]
Since $E_R(\mathbb Q)\cong E_{\widehat R}(\mathbb Q)$, one has the isomorphisms
\[
\mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n)\cong H^1\mathrm{Hom}_R(C,\mathbf I\langle n\rangle) \cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\widehat R}(H_0(Q)/t^nH_0(Q),E_R(\mathbb Q)).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Q}, choose a nonempty set $\Lambda$ such that $H_0(Q)\cong\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$ is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]$-modules.
Hence one has
\begin{align*}
    \mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n)
&\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}
\bigl(H_0(Q)/t^nH_0(Q),V\bigr)
\cong\prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]}
\bigl(\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/t^n\mathbb Q[\![t]\!],V\bigr)\\
&\cong \prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
t^{-n}\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]
\cong \prod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
\mathbb Q[\![t]\!]/t^n\mathbb Q[\![t]\!].
\end{align*}
This product is annihilated by $t^n$ but not by $t^{n-1}$, proving the assertions.

label: c:open-adjoints
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $u_\ast : \mathcal A_U \to \mathcal A_X$ admits an exact left adjoint, it preserves injective objects.
Hence $u_\ast : \mathcal T_U \to \mathcal T_X$ is well-defined.
By construction, $u_\ast$ preserves suspensions and conesm and thus is a triangle functor.
By \cite[Theorem~A.3]{EfimovPositselski}, $u^\ast$ also preserves injective objects.
Again the termwise application induces a triangle functor
$u^\ast:\mathcal T_X\to\mathcal T_U$.


The unit and counit of the adjunction $u^\ast\dashv u_\ast$ descend to the homotopy categories, where they still satisfy the triangle identities.
Hence $u^\ast\dashv u_\ast$ between $\mathcal T_X$ and $\mathcal T_U$.

Since $\mathcal A_U$ is a locally Noetherian Grothendieck category,
$\mathcal T_U$ is compactly generated by
\cite[Proposition~2.3]{Krause2005}.
Coproducts in $\mathcal T_U$ and $\mathcal T_X$ are computed degreewise.
Since $u_\ast:\mathcal A_U\to\mathcal A_X$ preserves coproducts,
so does the induced triangle functor
$u_\ast:\mathcal T_U\to\mathcal T_X$.
Thus $u_\ast : \mathcal T_U\to\mathcal T_X$ admits a right adjoint by Brown representability \cite[Proposition~3.3\textup{(1)}]{Krause2005}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
It is not necessarily that $u_\ast : \mathcal A_U \to \mathcal A_X$ admits a right adjoint.
For instance, consider $X = \operatorname{spec} k[x,y]$ and $U = X \setminus \{(x,y)\}$.
    Hence we denote the right adjoint of $u_\ast : \mathcal T_U \to \mathcal T_X$ by $u^\times$ rather then $u^!$.
head: environment

label: c:pushforward-acyclicity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:pushforward-acyclicity}
The functor $u_\ast:\mathcal T_U\to\mathcal T_X$ preserves and reflects total acyclicity, i.e., for every $I\in\mathcal T_U$, $u_\ast I$ is totally acyclic if and only if $I$ is totally acyclic.
head: environment

label: eq:C-local-acyclicity
title: Proof
body_md:
Let $I$ be an acyclic complex of injective objects on $U$.
To see that $u_\ast I$ is acyclic, it suffices to show for each affine open subscheme $V \subseteq X$ that $(u_\ast I)|_V$ is acyclic.
Write $V\cong\mathrm{Spec}(R)$. Then $\Gamma(V,-):\mathrm{QCoh}(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Mod}_R$ is an equivalence by \cite[Chapter~II, Corollary~5.5]{Hartshorne1977}.
Thus
\begin{align}
\mathcal H^n\bigl((u_\ast I)|_V\bigr)=0 & \iff \Gamma\!\left(V,
\mathcal H^n\bigl((u_\ast I)|_V\bigr)\right)=0 
\iff H^n\!\left(\Gamma\bigl(V,(u_\ast I)|_V\bigr)\right)=0\notag\\
&\iff H^n\bigl(\Gamma(U\cap V,I)\bigr)=0
\iff H^1(U\cap V,Z^{n-1}I)=0 \notag\\
&\iff \cdots 
\iff H^q(U\cap V,Z^{n-q}I)=0 \quad (\exists q \geq 1).\label{eq:C-local-acyclicity}
\end{align}
Now fix an affine open $V=\mathrm{Spec}\,R\subseteq X$.
If $U \cap V=\varnothing$, there is nothing to prove on $V$.
Otherwise, $U \cap V$ is quasi-compact, so choose $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in R$ such that
\[
D_V(f_i)\subseteq U \cap V,\qquad W=\bigcup_{i=1}^m D_V(f_i).
\]
For $1\leq i_0<\cdots<i_p\leq m$, write
\[
(U \cap V)_{i_0\cdots i_p}
=D_V(f_{i_0})\cap\cdots\cap D_V(f_{i_p})
=D_V(f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}).
\]
For $\mathcal F\in\mathrm{QCoh}(U \cap V)$, the \v Cech complex has terms
\[
C^p(\mathcal F)=
\prod_{1\leq i_0<\cdots<i_p\leq m}
\Gamma((U \cap V)_{i_0\cdots i_p},\mathcal F)
\qquad(0\leq p\leq m-1),
\]
and zero terms otherwise. Its differential is
\[
(\delta^p s)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}
=\sum_{a=0}^{p+1}(-1)^a
s_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_a}\cdots i_{p+1}}
\big|_{(U \cap V)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}}.
\]
Thus it is the finite complex
\begin{multline*}
0\longrightarrow\prod_{i=1}^m\Gamma(D_V(f_i),\mathcal F)
\longrightarrow\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq m}\Gamma(D_V(f_if_j),\mathcal F) \longrightarrow \cdots \\
\cdots \longrightarrow \prod_{i=1}^{m}
\Gamma\!\bigg(D_V\!\big(\prod_{j\ne i}f_j\big),\mathcal F\bigg)\longrightarrow
\Gamma(D_V(f_1\cdots f_m),\mathcal F)\longrightarrow0,
\end{multline*}
with the first nonzero term in degree zero.
All intersections $W_{i_0\cdots i_p}$ are affine, and $W$ is separated as an open subscheme of the affine scheme $V$.
By \cite[Chapter~III, Theorem~4.5]{Hartshorne1977}, this complex computes sheaf cohomology.
Hence $H^q(U \cap V, \mathcal F)=0$ for each $q \geq m$.
Put $\mathcal F = (Z^{n-m} I)|_{U \cap V}$.
Then $H^m(U \cap V, Z^{n-m}I)=0$, satisfying \eqref{eq:C-local-acyclicity}.

To see that $u_\ast I$ is totally acyclic, for any injective object $E\in\mathcal A_X$, the object $u^\ast E$ is injective in $\mathcal A_U$, and adjunction gives an isomorphism of complexes
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_X}(E,u_\ast I)
\cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_U}(u^\ast E,I).
\]
The latter is acyclic since $I$ is totally acyclic.
Thus $u_\ast I$ is totally acyclic.


Conversely, suppose that $u_\ast I$ is totally acyclic.
Since $u^\ast$ is exact and $u^\ast u_\ast I\cong I$, the complex $I$ is acyclic.
For every injective object $E\in\mathcal A_U$, $u_\ast E$ is injective in $\mathcal A_X$, since $u_\ast$ admits an exact left adjoint.
Full faithfulness of $u_\ast$ gives an isomorphism of complexes
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_U}(E,I)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_X}(u_\ast E,u_\ast I).
\]
Since $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_X}(u_\ast E,u_\ast I)$ is acyclic, $I$ is also totally acyclic.
head: environment

label: c:right-adjoint-acyclicity
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:right-adjoint-acyclicity}
The functor $u^\times : \mathcal T_X \to \mathcal T_U$ preserves total acyclicity.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We show that $u^\times I$ is acyclic whenever $I\in\mathcal T_X$ is acyclic.
We first treat affine $X$, then the case $X=U\cup V$ with $V$ affine.
The general case follows by adjoining the members of a finite affine cover one at a time.

Suppose first that $X=\mathrm{Spec}(R)$.
Choose a finite principal cover $U=\bigcup_{i=1}^mD(f_i)$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity}.
Let $\mathcal O _U$ be the structral sheaf.
Fix a bounded-below injective resolution $\mathcal O_U\to\iota\mathcal O_U$.
For every $J\in\mathcal T_U$, one has
\begin{align*}
    H^n\Gamma(U,u^\times I) & \cong H^n \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_U}(\mathcal O_U, u^\times I) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A_U)}(\mathcal O_U, u^\times I[n])\\
    & \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_U} (\iota \mathcal O_U, u^\times I[n]) \cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X} (u_\ast \iota \mathcal O_U, I[n]) .
\end{align*}
Under the equivalence $\Gamma(X,-) : \mathrm{QCoh}(X)\simeq\mathrm{Mod}_R$, the bounded-below complex $u_\ast\iota\mathcal O_U$ is an injective resolution of the finite \v Cech complex (with first term in degree zero)
\[
 C^\bullet=
 \left[
 \prod_iR_{f_i}\longrightarrow
 \prod_{i<j}R_{f_if_j}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow
 R_{f_1\cdots f_m}
 \right].
\]
Hence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(u_\ast\iota\mathcal O_U,I[n])
 \cong H^n\mathrm{Hom}_R(C^\bullet,I)$.
For each $f\in R$, $R_f$ has free resolution
\[
 0\longrightarrow\coprod_{k\geq0}R
 \xrightarrow{\ e_k\mapsto e_k-fe_{k+1}\ }
 \coprod_{k\geq0}R\longrightarrow R_f\longrightarrow0.
\]
Hence $\mathrm{pd}_R R_f\leq1$.
It follows from dimension shift that
\[
 H^n\mathrm{Hom}_R(R_f,I)
 \cong\mathrm{Ext}_R^1(R_f,Z^{n-1}I)
 \cong\mathrm{Ext}_R^2(R_f,Z^{n-2}I)=0.
\]
Since $C^\bullet$ is bounded, $\mathrm{Hom}_R(C^\bullet,I)$ is acyclic by induction on length.
The previous isomorphisms shows that $\Gamma(U,u^\times I)$ is acyclic.
Since $U \subseteq X$ is open, $\Gamma(U,u^\times I)=\Gamma(X,u_\ast u^\times I)$.
Note that and $\Gamma(X,-)$ is an equivalence, $u_\ast u^\times I$ is acyclic.
Since $u^\ast$ is exact and $u_\ast$ is fully faithful, $u^\times I \cong u^\ast u_\ast u^\times I$ is acyclic.

Suppose next that $X=U\cup V$ with $V$ affine, and denote the inclusions by
\[
\xymatrix@C=2cm@R=.0cm{
& \ U\  \ar[dr]^-u & \\
U\cap V \
\ar[ur]^-{u'}
\ar[rr]^-z
\ar[dr]_-{v'}
&& \ U\cup V\\
& \ V \  \ar[ur]_-v &
}
\]
For an acyclic $I\in\mathcal T_X$, the Mayer--Vietoris sequence $ 0\to I\to u_\ast u^\ast I\oplus v_\ast v^\ast I \to z_\ast z^\ast I\to 0$ splits in each degree, since its terms are injective.
It gives a distinguished triangle
\[
 I\longrightarrow u_\ast u^\ast I\oplus v_\ast v^\ast I
 \longrightarrow z_\ast z^\ast I\longrightarrow I[1]
\]
in $\mathcal T_X$.
Since $u_\ast$ is fully faithful, $u^\times u_\ast\cong1$.
Open base change gives $v^\ast u_\ast\cong v'_\ast u'^\ast$.
Taking the right adjoints gives $u^\times v_\ast\cong u'_\ast v'^\times$.
Together with $z_\ast=u_\ast u'_\ast$, these yield
\[
 u^\times u_\ast u^\ast I\cong u^\ast I,\qquad
 u^\times v_\ast v^\ast I\cong u'_\ast v'^\times v^\ast I,\qquad
 u^\times z_\ast z^\ast I\cong u'_\ast z^\ast I.
\]
All three complexes are acyclic: 
restrictions $u^\ast$, $v^\ast$ and $z^\ast$ are exact; 
$v'^\times$ preserves acyclicity by the affine case;
$u'_\ast$ preserves acyclicity by the proof of Lemma~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity}.
Applying $u^\times$ to the displayed triangle therefore shows that $u^\times I$ is acyclic.

To see that $u^\times I$ is totally acyclic when $I$ is totally acyclic, regard an injective object $E\in\mathcal A_U$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero.
For every $n\in\mathbb Z$,
\[
 \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_U}(E,u^\times I[n])
 \cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(u_\ast E,I[n])=0,
\]
since $u_\ast E$ is injective.
These are the cohomology groups of $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal A_U}(E,u^\times I)$.
Together with the acyclicity already proved, this gives total acyclicity.

label: c:tac-adjunction
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemmas~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity} and~\ref{c:right-adjoint-acyclicity}, $u_\ast$ and $u^\times$ restrict to acyclic complexes.
For arbitrary $A\in\mathcal S_U$ and $B\in\mathcal S_X$ the adjunction gives natural isomorphisms
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal S_X}(\widetilde{u_\ast}A,B)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(u_\ast A,B)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_U}(A,u^\times B)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal S_U}(A,\widetilde{u^\times}B).
\]
Thus $\widetilde{u_\ast}\dashv\widetilde{u^\times}$, and compatibility with the inclusions holds by definition.
head: environment

label: rmk:uleft
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk:uleft}
By \cite[Lemma~7.3]{Krause2005}, the inclusion
$i_U{}_{\ast}:\mathcal S_U\to\mathcal T_U$
admits a left adjoint $i_U{}^\ast$.
Hence $\widetilde{u_\ast}$ has a left adjoint $i_U{}^\ast u^\ast i_X{}_\ast$.
This adjoint coincides with the restriction of $u^\ast$ if and only if $u^\ast$ preserves totally acyclic complexes; this does not hold in general.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md:
This example shows that $u^\ast$ need not preserve totally acyclic complexes.
Retain Example~\ref{thm:main}, take $X = \mathrm{Spec}(R) = \{\mathfrak m_R, \mathfrak n\}$ and $U = D(t) = \{\mathfrak n\} \cong \mathrm{Spec}(R[t^{-1}])$.
Then $u_\ast : \mathrm{Mod}_{R[t^{-1}]} \to \mathrm{Mod}_R$ is the forgetful functor with left adjoint
\[
u^\ast : \mathrm{Mod}_R \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mod}_{R[t^{-1}]}, \qquad M \longmapsto M[t^{-1}] = R[t^{-1}] \otimes _R M.
\]
Then take $\prod_{n \geq 1} \mathbf I\langle n \rangle \in \mathcal S_X$, where $\prod_{n \geq 1} G_n = \prod_{n \geq 1} Z^0 (\mathbf I\langle n \rangle) \cong  Z^0 (\prod_{n \geq 1} \mathbf I\langle n \rangle) \in \mathcal {GI}(R)$.

Note that $u^\ast$ is the localisation with respect to the multiplication system $\{1,t,t^2, \ldots\}$.
Since $R$ is Noetherian and $C$ is finitely generated, one has caninonical isomorphisms
\[
\mathrm{Ext}^1_{u^\ast R} \left(u^\ast C, u^\ast\prod_{n \geq 1} G_n \right) \cong 
u^\ast\mathrm{Ext}^1_{R} \left( C, \prod_{n \geq 1} G_n \right) \cong u^\ast \left(\prod_{n\geq1}\mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n)\right)
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:Tn}, $t^{n} \mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n) =0$ whereas $t^{n-1} \mathrm{Ext}_R^1(C,G_n) \neq 0$. 
Hence the above is non-zero.
In particular, since $u^\ast C$ is injective, $u^\ast\prod_{n \geq 1} G_n$ is not Gorenstein injective.
It follows that $u^\ast\left(\prod_{n\geq1}\mathbf I\langle n\rangle\right)$ is not totally acyclic.

Therefore $u^\ast$ need not preserve totoally acyclic complexes.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The implications $\textup{(1)}\Longrightarrow\textup{(5)}\Longrightarrow\textup{(6)}\Longrightarrow\textup{(4)}\Longrightarrow\textup{(3)}$ are immediate.

\noindent\textit{$(2)\Longrightarrow(1)$.}
Suppose $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_X)$ is covering and let $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence}, $\mathcal S_X$ is closed under coproducts. 
Let $(I_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be a family in $\mathcal S_U$.
By Lemma~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity}, each $u_\ast I_\alpha$ is totally acyclic.
By Lemma~\ref{c:open-adjoints}, $u_\ast$ preserves coproducts, 
thus $u_\ast\!\left(\coprod_{\alpha\in\Lambda} I_\alpha\right) \cong\coprod_{\alpha\in\Lambda} u_\ast I_\alpha$.
Again by Lemma~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity}, $\coprod_{\alpha\in\Lambda} I_\alpha\in \mathcal S_U$.
Hence $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_U)$ is covering by Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence}.

\noindent\textit{$(3)\Longrightarrow(2)$.}
Quasi-compactness reduces the given cover to a finite subcover, so it suffices to treat $X=U\cup V$.
Write $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, $v:V\hookrightarrow X$, $u':U\cap V\hookrightarrow U$, $v':U\cap V\hookrightarrow V$ and $z:U\cap V\hookrightarrow X$ for the inclusions.
By $\textup{(2)}\Longrightarrow\textup{(1)}$, the covering property also holds on $U\cap V$.
Denote the counit of $w_\ast\dashv w^\times$ by $\varepsilon^w$.

For every $I\in\mathcal T_X$, one has a distinguished triangle
\begin{equation}
z_\ast z^\times I
\xlongrightarrow{\begin{psmallmatrix}
(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\
-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I
\end{psmallmatrix}} \label{eq:C-cone-triangle}
u_\ast u^\times I\oplus v_\ast v^\times I
\xlongrightarrow{\iota}
\mathrm{Cone}\begin{psmallmatrix}
(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\
-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I
\end{psmallmatrix}
\longrightarrow (z_\ast z^\times I)[1].
\end{equation}
Then we claim that $\mathrm{Cone}\begin{psmallmatrix}(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I\end{psmallmatrix}
 \cong I$.

Apply $u^\times$ to $\begin{psmallmatrix}
(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\
-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I
\end{psmallmatrix}: z_\ast z^\times I
\to
u_\ast u^\times I\oplus v_\ast v^\times I$, one has the natural isomorphisms $u^\times z_\ast z^\times \cong u^\times u_\ast u'{}_\ast z^\times \cong u'{}_\ast z^\times $, $u^\times u_\ast u^\times = u^\times$, $u^\times v_\ast v^\times \cong u'_\ast v'^\times v^\times \cong u'_\ast z^\times$, $u^\times (u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times) \cong \varepsilon ^{u'} u^\times$, and $u^\times(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)\cong u'{}_\ast(v'^\times\varepsilon^{v'})v^\times$.
Since $v'{}_\ast$ is fully faithful, the unit of $v'{}_\ast \dashv v'^\times$ is invertible and thus $v'^\times \varepsilon ^{v'}$ is a natural isomorphism by triangle identity.
Applying $u^\times$ to \eqref{eq:C-cone-triangle} above gives the distinguished triangle
\[
u'_\ast z^\times I
\xlongrightarrow{\begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\1\end{psmallmatrix}}
u^\times I\oplus u'_\ast z^\times I
\xlongrightarrow{\begin{psmallmatrix}1&-(\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\end{psmallmatrix}}
u^\times I\xlongrightarrow{0}(u'_\ast z^\times I)[1]
\]
with an isomorphism $\varphi : u^\times I \cong u^\times \mathrm{Cone}\begin{psmallmatrix}
(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\
-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I
\end{psmallmatrix}$ 

Since $(\varepsilon^u)_I\circ(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I =(\varepsilon^z)_I = (\varepsilon^v)_I\circ(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I$,
one has
\[
\begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^u)_I&(\varepsilon^v)_I\end{psmallmatrix}
\circ
\begin{psmallmatrix}
(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\
-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I
\end{psmallmatrix}=0, \qquad \begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^u)_I&(\varepsilon^v)_I\end{psmallmatrix} : u_\ast u^\times I\oplus v_\ast v^\times I \longrightarrow I.
\]
Hence $\begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^u)_I&(\varepsilon^v)_I\end{psmallmatrix}$ factors through $\iota$ via
\[
h:\mathrm{Cone}\begin{psmallmatrix}
(u_\ast\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\
-(v_\ast\varepsilon^{v'}v^\times)_I
\end{psmallmatrix}\longrightarrow I,
\qquad
h\circ\iota=
\begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^u)_I&(\varepsilon^v)_I\end{psmallmatrix},
\]
After applying $u^\times$, the following diagram commutes
\[
\xymatrix@C=2cm@R=.7cm{
u'_\ast z^\times I
\ar[r]^-{\begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\\1\end{psmallmatrix}}
& u^\times I\oplus u'_\ast z^\times I
\ar[r]^-{\begin{psmallmatrix}1&-(\varepsilon^{u'}u^\times)_I\end{psmallmatrix}}
\ar[d]_-{u^\times\!\left(\begin{psmallmatrix}(\varepsilon^u)_I&(\varepsilon^v)_I\end{psmallmatrix}\right)}
& u^\times I
\ar[r]^-{0}
\ar[dl]^-{(u^\times h)\circ\varphi}
& (u'_\ast z^\times I)[1]
\\
& u^\times I
}
\]
Thus $u^\times h$ is an isomorphism.

Similarly $v^\times h$ is an isomorphism.
Put $K = \mathrm{Cone}(h)$.
It follows that $u^\times K = 0$ and $v^\times K = 0$.
Hence $z^\times K = 0$.
For each $A \in \mathcal T_X$, apply $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(-,K)$ to Mayer--Vietoris triangle $A\longrightarrow u_\ast u^\ast A\oplus v_\ast v^\ast A
\longrightarrow z_\ast z^\ast A\longrightarrow A[1]$.
Then one has a long exact sequence
\[
\longrightarrow
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(A, K)[-1]
\longrightarrow 
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(z_\ast z^\ast A, K)
\longrightarrow
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(u_\ast u^\ast A\oplus v_\ast v^\ast A, K)
\longrightarrow
\]
By adjunctions one has $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(A, K) = 0$.
In particular, taking $A=K$ gives that
$\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(K,K)=0$, hence $1_K=0$.
Thus $K$ is contractible.
Consequently, $h$ is an isomorphism, proving the claim.

Now let $(I_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\Lambda}$ be a family in $\mathcal S_X$.
For $w\in\{u,v,z\}$, Proposition~\ref{c:tac-adjunction} shows that $w^\times I_\alpha$ is totally acyclic.
By assumption and the implication $(2) \implies (1)$, $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_U)$, $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_U)$ and $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_{U \cap V})$ are covering classes, and thus Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence} shows that $\coprod_\alpha w^\times I_\alpha$ is totally acyclic.
Lemma~\ref{c:open-adjoints} allows this coproduct to pass through $w_\ast$, and Lemma~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity} shows that
\[
 \coprod_\alpha w_\ast w^\times I_\alpha
 \cong w_\ast\!\left(\coprod_\alpha w^\times I_\alpha\right)
 \in\mathcal S_X.
\]
Taking coproducts of the triangles \eqref{eq:C-cone-triangle} for each $\alpha$, and using the isomorphisms of cones and $I_\alpha$ proved above, we obtain a distinguished triangle
\[
\coprod_\alpha z_\ast z^\times I_\alpha
\longrightarrow
\left(\coprod_\alpha u_\ast u^\times I_\alpha\right)
\oplus
\left(\coprod_\alpha v_\ast v^\times I_\alpha\right)
\longrightarrow
\coprod_\alpha I_\alpha
\longrightarrow
\left(\coprod_\alpha z_\ast z^\times I_\alpha\right)[1].
\]
The first two terms belong to $\mathcal S_X$ by the preceding argument.
Thus $\coprod_\alpha I_\alpha \in \mathcal S_X$.
Hence $\mathcal S_X$ is closed under coproducts, and Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence} implies that $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_X)$ is covering.

This completes the proof.

title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
For $A\in\mathcal D_X$, choose a \emph{$K$-flat resolution} $F\to A$ by flat quasi-coherent sheaves, meaning that $F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}-$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms.
For $I\in\mathcal T_X$, define
\[
 A\star I=\mathrm{Tot}^{\coprod}(F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}I),
 \qquad
 (A\star I)^n=\coprod_{p+q=n}F^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}I^q,
\]
with differential $d_F\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_I$ on $F^p\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}I^q$.

Since $X$ is Noetherian, tensoring an injective quasi-coherent sheaf with a flat one gives an injective sheaf, and coproducts of injectives are injective.
Thus $A\star I$ has injective terms.
The construction is independent of the chosen $K$-flat resolution \cite[\S2.8]{BILMP2026}.
head: environment

label: lem:PIS
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:PIS}
    For a perfect complex $P$ and $I \in \mathcal S_X$, one has $P \star I \in \mathcal S_X$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $q_X(P\star I)\cong P\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}q_XI=0$, $P\star I$ is acyclic.

Put $P^\vee=\mathbf R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(P,\mathcal O_X)$, which is again perfect \cite[\S2.8]{BILMP2026}.
Hence
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(E,(P\star I)[n])
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal T_X}(P^\vee\star E,I[n])
=0
\qquad(n\in\mathbb Z),
\]
The final equality holds since $P^\vee \star E$ is bounded injective complex.
Thus $P\star I\in\mathcal S_X$.
