label: cor:ais
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For fixed $I\in\mathcal S_X$, the subcategory $\{A\in\mathcal D_X\mid A\star I\in\mathcal S_X\}$ is localising, since $-\star I$ is exact and preserves coproducts.
By Lemma~\ref{lem:PIS} this subcategory contains every perfect complex, hence equals $\mathrm{Loc}_{\mathcal D_X}\bigl(\mathrm{Perf}(X)\bigr)=\mathcal D_X$.
head: environment

label: c:tensor-open-localisation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:tensor-open-localisation}
For every $I\in\mathcal T_X$, there is a natural isomorphism
\[
 (\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I\cong u_\ast u^\ast I
 \quad\text{in }\mathcal T_X.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $u$ is an open immersion, the derived counit gives
\[
u^\ast\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U
\simeq u^\ast u_\ast(\iota\mathcal O_U)
\cong\iota\mathcal O_U
\simeq\mathcal O_U.
\]
Hence there are natural isomorphisms in $\mathcal T_U$
\[
u^\ast((\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I)
\cong(u^\ast \mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star(u^\ast I)
\cong \mathcal O_U\star(u^\ast I)
\cong u^\ast I,
\]
whose composition corresponds to $\alpha_I:(\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I\to u_\ast u^\ast I$ by adjunction $u^\ast \dashv u_\ast$.

The case $U=\varnothing$ is immediate.
For affine $X=\mathrm{Spec}(R)$, use the finite principal \v Cech complex $C^\bullet$ from the proof of Lemma~\ref{c:right-adjoint-acyclicity}.
It is bounded and flat, represents $\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U$, and hence computes $(\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I=\mathrm{Tot}(C^\bullet\otimes_R I)$.
The augmentation \v Cech double complex
\[
 \beta_I:u_\ast u^\ast I\longrightarrow\mathrm{Tot}(C^\bullet\otimes_R I)
\]
has finite exact horizontal rows, i.e., $(u_\ast u^\ast I)^n \to \mathrm{Tot}(C^\bullet \otimes _R I^n)$ is finite exact for each $n$.
For every $n\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\leq p<m$, Lemma~\ref{c:open-adjoints} gives
\[
u_\ast u^\ast I^n\in\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A_X,
\qquad
C^p\otimes_R I^n
=\coprod_{i_0<\cdots<i_p}(I^n)_{f_{i_0}\cdots f_{i_p}}
\in\mathrm{Inj}\,\mathcal A_X,
\]
where we identify $R$-modules with quasi-coherent sheaves on $X=\mathrm{Spec}(R)$.
Thus, for every $n\in\mathbb Z$, the following sequence is split exact in $\mathrm{Mod}_R$:
\[
0\longrightarrow\Gamma(U,I^n|_U)
\longrightarrow C^0\otimes_R I^n
\longrightarrow C^1\otimes_R I^n
\longrightarrow\cdots
\longrightarrow C^{m-1}\otimes_R I^n
\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus $\mathrm{Cone}(\beta_I)$ is contractible, and equivalently $\beta_I$ is a homotopy equivalence.

Note that in $\mathcal D_U$, one has the retract
\[
1_{\mathcal O_U} = \big[\mathcal O_U
\xrightarrow{\text{Čech augmentation}}
u^\ast\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U
\xrightarrow{\text{counit}}
\mathcal O_U\big].
\]
Applying $- \star (u^\ast I)$ yields that 

\[
\xymatrix@C=1.5cm@R=.7cm{
\mathcal O_U\star(u^\ast I)
\ar[r]
\ar@/^1.5pc/@{=}[rr]
\ar[d]_-{\cong}
& (u^\ast\mathbf R u_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star(u^\ast I)
\ar[r]
\ar[d]^-{\cong}
& \mathcal O_U\star(u^\ast I)
\ar[d]^-{\cong}
\\
u^\ast I
\ar[r]^-{u^\ast\beta_I}
& u^\ast\bigl((\mathbf R u_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I\bigr)
\ar[r]^-{u^\ast\alpha_I}
& u^\ast I
}
\]
Then applying $u_\ast$ and $u_\ast u^\ast \cong 1$ give that $\alpha_I\beta_I=1$, thus $\alpha_I=\beta_I^{-1}$.

For general $X$, let $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ be an affine open immersion and put $w:U\cap V\hookrightarrow V$.
Then open base change tensor action with restriction identify $v^\ast\alpha_I$ with $\alpha_{v^\ast I}$
\[
\xymatrix@C=1.2cm@R=.7cm{
v^\ast\bigl((\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I\bigr)
\ar[r]^-{\cong}
\ar[d]_-{v^\ast\alpha_I}
& (v^\ast\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star(v^\ast I)
\ar[r]^-{\cong}
& (\mathbf Rw_\ast\mathcal O_{U\cap V})\star(v^\ast I)
\ar[d]^-{\alpha_{v^\ast I}}
\\
v^\ast u_\ast u^\ast I
\ar[r]^-{\cong}
& w_\ast(I|_{U\cap V})
\ar[r]^-{\cong}
& w_\ast w^\ast(v^\ast I)
}
\]
The affine case shows that $v^\ast\alpha_I$ is a homotopy equivalence, and so is $\alpha_{v^\ast I}$.
Restriction commutes with mapping cones, so $v^\ast\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)
\cong\mathrm{Cone}(v^\ast\alpha_I)
\simeq0$.
Thus $\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)$ is acyclic on any affine open cover, and hence $\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)$ is acyclic.
Since $v^\ast$ is exact, $v^\ast Z^n\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I) \cong Z^n\bigl(v^\ast\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)\bigr)$ is a direct summand of a term of  $v^\ast\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)$, and thus is injective.
By \cite[Proposition~B.1]{CoupekStovicek2020}, each $Z^n\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)$ is injective on $X$.
Consequently, the short exact sequences
\[
0\longrightarrow Z^n\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)
\longrightarrow\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)^n
\longrightarrow Z^{n+1}\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)
\longrightarrow0
\]
split for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.
Hence $\mathrm{Cone}(\alpha_I)$ is contractible, and $\alpha_I$ is an isomorphism in $\mathcal T_X$.

title: Proof
body_md:
When $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_X)$ is covering, Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence} shows that $\mathcal S_X$ is localising.
Then by Corollary~\ref{cor:ais} and Lemma~\ref{c:tensor-open-localisation}, one has
\[
 u_\ast u^\ast I\cong(\mathbf Ru_\ast\mathcal O_U)\star I\in\mathcal S_X
 \qquad(I\in\mathcal S_X).
\]
Since $u_\ast$ reflects total acyclicity by Lemma~\ref{c:pushforward-acyclicity}, $u^\ast I\in\mathcal S_U$.
Together with Proposition~\ref{c:tac-adjunction}, $u^\ast \dashv u_\ast \dashv u^\times$ restrict to the full subcategories $\mathcal S_X$ and $\mathcal S_U$, yielding $\widetilde{u^\ast}\dashv\widetilde{u_\ast}\dashv\widetilde{u^\times}$.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:locality}, $\mathcal{GI}(\mathcal A_U)$ is covering.
Thus, for $Y=X,U$, Theorem~\ref{thm:equivalence} supplies the right adjoint $i_Y{}^!$.
Denote by $D_{\mathrm{qc}}(\mathcal O_X)$ the full subcategory of the derived category of all $\mathcal O_X$-modules consisting of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology. By \cite[Theorem~3.1.1]{BondalVanDenBergh},
$D_{\mathrm{qc}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ is compactly generated;
the equivalence
$\mathcal D_Y\simeq D_{\mathrm{qc}}(\mathcal O_Y)$
of \cite[Theorem~1.2]{HallNeemanRydh} shows that $\mathcal D_Y$ is compactly generated.
Hence \cite[Lemma~7.3]{Krause2005} gives the left adjoint $i_Y{}^\ast$, and Proposition~\ref{prop:tac-recollement} gives the recollements.

Since all three ambient functors preserve the totally acyclic subcategories, they descend to the Verdier quotients.
The adjunction units and counits descend with their triangle identities, giving $\widehat{u^\ast}\dashv\widehat{u_\ast}\dashv\widehat{u^\times}$.

The first three displayed squares commute by the definitions of the restricted functors, and the last three by the definitions of the quotient functors.

title: Lemma
body_md:
For each $i \in \mathbb N_+$, $\mathfrak p_i=(t_i^3,t_i^4,t_i^5)$ is a prime ideal of $B_0$.
Then 
\[
\{P\in\mathrm{Spec}(B_0):P\cap U=\varnothing\}
=\{(0)\}\cup\{\mathfrak p_i:i\ge1\},
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first claim that any nonzero prime ideal of $B_0$ with empty intersection with $U$ is contained in some $\mathfrak p_i$.
Otherwise, suppose that there exists a counterexample $P$, that is, $P \not\subseteq \mathfrak p_i$ for all $i \in \mathbb N_+$.
Then for any nonzero $a \in P$, put $F(a) = \{i \in \mathbb N_+\mid a \in \mathfrak p_i\}$.
By colimit construction, $a$ lies in the image of $D_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes D_m$ for some $m$ and thus $F(a)$ is finite.
Then by prime avoidance \cite[Proposition~1.11\textup{(i)}]{AtiyahMacdonald1969},
choose $b\in P\setminus\bigcup_{i\in F}\mathfrak p_i$.
Hence for each $i \in \mathbb N_+$, one has $a \notin \mathfrak p_i$ or $b \notin \mathfrak p_i$. 
Again $a$ and $b$ lies in the image of $D_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes D_n$ for some $n \in \mathbb N_+$, thus neither belongs to $\mathfrak p_i$ for $i > n$.
In this case, there is $\lambda \in \mathbb Q$ such that $(a + \lambda b) \notin \mathfrak p_i$ for each $i \in \mathbb N_+$.
Thus $(a + \lambda b) \in U$, a contradiction.

Then fix a nonzero prime ideal $P$ of $B_0$.
The above discussion gives $P \subseteq \mathfrak p_i$ for some $i \in \mathbb N_+$.
Since $K_i [t_i^3, t_i^4, t_i^5] \cong K_i[t_i^3] \oplus t_i^4 K_i[t_i^3] \oplus t_i^5 K_i[t_i^3]$ as a $K_i[t_i^3]$-module, $K_i [t_i^3, t_i^4, t_i^5]$ is an integral domain with $\dim K_i [t_i^3, t_i^4, t_i^5] = \dim K_i [t_i^3] = 1$.
Thus the local ring 
\[
(B_0)_{\mathfrak p_i} \cong K_i[t_i^3,t_i^4,t_i^5]_{(t_i^3,t_i^4,t_i^5)}
\]
is a one-dimensional domain.
Clearly $P$ is sent to a nonzero prime ideal and thus is the maximal ideal.
By assumption $P \subseteq \mathfrak p_i$, one has $P=\mathfrak p_i$.

Each $\mathfrak p_i$ and $0$ are disjoint from $U$, proving this lemma.

label: c:lem:ringproperties
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{c:lem:ringproperties}
The prime spectrum of $S$ is
\[
\mathrm{Spec}(S) = \{\mathfrak n\} \cup \{\mathfrak m_i\}_{i \in \mathbb N_+},
\qquad \mathfrak m_i = (t_i^3,t_i^4,t_i^5,u,v).
\]
head: environment

label: c:lem:S-localisations
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:S-localisations}
The localisations of $S$ are
\[
S_{\mathfrak m_i}\cong B_{\mathfrak m_{B,i}}[u,v]/(u,v)^2,\qquad
S_{\mathfrak n}\cong K[u,v]/(u,v)^2.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $\mathfrak q\in\mathrm{Spec}(B)$, localising the coefficients gives $B_{\mathfrak q}[u,v]/(u,v)^2$, a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}+(u,v)$.
Thus this ring is $S_{\mathfrak qS+\mathfrak n}$.
Taking $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak m_{B,i}$ and $\mathfrak q=(0)$, and using $B_{(0)}=K$, gives the assertions.
head: environment

label: c:lem:S-properties
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:S-properties}
The ring $S$ is Noetherian and Cohen--Macaulay of dimension one.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By computation of $\mathrm{Spec}(S)$, $S$ has Krull dimension $1$.
Since every prime ideal of $B$ is finitely generated by the preceding description, $B$ is Noetherian by Cohen's theorem \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Matsumura1989}.
Since $S$ is finite free of rank $3$ over $B$, $S$ is Noetherian.
By Lemma~\ref{c:lem:S-localisations}, each $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$ is free over the domain $B_{\mathfrak m_{B,i}}$, so $t_i^3$ is a nonzerodivisor in its maximal ideal.
Hence it has nonzero depth and thus coincides with the Krull dimension $1$.
The remaining localisation $S_{\mathfrak n}$ is again Artinian and therefore $S$ is Cohen--Macaulay.

label: c:prop:local-dualising
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{c:prop:local-dualising}
Dualising complexes for $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$ and $S_{\mathfrak n}$ are respectively the modules
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{K_i[t_i^3]_{(t_i^3)}}
\bigl(S_{\mathfrak m_i},K_i[t_i^3]_{(t_i^3)}\bigr),\qquad
\mathrm{Hom}_K(K[u,v]/(u,v)^2,K),
\]
both are viewed as complexes concentrated in degree zero.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider either of the pairs \(
(\Lambda,T)=
\bigl(K_i[t_i^3]_{(t_i^3)},S_{\mathfrak m_i}\bigr)
\quad\text{or}\quad
\bigl(K,K[u,v]/(u,v)^2\bigr),\) and put $\omega=\mathrm{Hom}_\Lambda(T,\Lambda)$.
In the first case, $T$ is finite free over $\Lambda$ with basis
\[
\{1,t_i^4,t_i^5,u,t_i^4u,t_i^5u,v,t_i^4v,t_i^5v\}.
\]
in the second case, it has basis $\{1,u,v\}$.
Thus $\omega$ is finite free over $\Lambda$.

Since $\Lambda$ is a discrete valuation ring or a field, it has an injective resolution of length at most one.
Applying $\mathrm{Hom}_\Lambda(T,-)$ gives an injective resolution of $\omega$ over $T$: exactness follows from the freeness of $T$, and injectivity follows from the adjunction
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_T\bigl(-,\mathrm{Hom}_\Lambda(T,J)\bigr)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_\Lambda(-,J).
\]
In particular, $\mathrm{id}_T\omega\leq1$.

Finally, the same adjunction gives
\[
\mathrm{Ext}_T^q(\omega,\omega)
\cong\mathrm{Ext}_\Lambda^q(\omega,\Lambda)=0
\qquad(q>0),
\]
and the homothety map is identified as
\[
T\longrightarrow\mathrm{Hom}_T(\omega,\omega)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_\Lambda(\omega,\Lambda), \qquad t \longmapsto \big(f \longmapsto f(t)\big)
\]
Thus $\omega$ is a dualising complex for $T$.

For every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, $\mathcal{GI}(S_{\mathfrak q})$ is covering.

title: Proof
body_md:

label: c:lem:genericinjective
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:genericinjective}
There are isomorphisms of $S$-modules
\[
\Omega\otimes_BK\cong\mathrm{Hom}_B(S,K)\cong E_S(S/\mathfrak n).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:J-injective}, every element outside $\mathfrak n$ acts injectively (thus invertibly) on $E_S(S/\mathfrak n)$, so \cite[Lemma~3.2.5]{BrunsHerzog} gives $E_S(S/\mathfrak n)\cong E_{S_{\mathfrak n}}(K)$.
By Lemma~\ref{c:lem:S-localisations}, $S_{\mathfrak n}=S\otimes_BK\cong K[u,v]/(u,v)^2$; applying Proposition~\ref{prop:finite-local-injective} to $K\to S_{\mathfrak n}$ yields
\[
E_S(S/\mathfrak n)\cong E_{S_{\mathfrak n}}(K)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_K(S_{\mathfrak n},K)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_B(S,K)\cong\Omega\otimes_BK.
\]
The last isomorphism uses finite freeness of $S$ over $B$.

label: c:lem:artin-periodic
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The duality $\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(-,\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*)\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{K_i}(-,K_i)$ makes $\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*$ an injective cogenerator.
For Noetherian rings, every injective $\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)$-module is a summand of coproduct of copies of $\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*$.

Set $I_i=\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(P_i,\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*)$.
Since the terms of $P_i$ are free, the terms of $I_i$ are products of the injective module $\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*$ and hence are injective.
Since $\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(-,\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*)$ is exact and  $P_i$ acyclic, $I_i$ is acyclic.
For any injective $\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)$-module $E$, the complex $E\otimes_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}P_i$ is a direct summand of a coproduct of copies of the acyclic complex $\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*\otimes_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}P_i$, so it is acyclic.
Thus
\[
\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(E,I_i)
\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}
\bigl(E\otimes_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}P_i,\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*\bigr).
\]
It follows that $\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(E,I_i)$ is acyclic.
Thus $I_i$ is totally acyclic.
Put $L_i=Z^0I_i$, one has \eqref{c:eq:Lperiodic}.
For $j\geq1$, the exactness of $\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(-,\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\bigr)^*)$ gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{Ext}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}^j(\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i^*\bigr),L_i)
&\cong H^j\mathrm{Hom}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}(\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i^*\bigr),I_i)\\
&\cong\mathrm{Hom}_{K_i}\bigl(H^{-j}(\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i^*\bigr)\otimes_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}P_i),K_i\bigr)\ne0.
\end{aligned}
\]
By the identification $S_{\mathfrak m_i}/t_i^3S_{\mathfrak m_i}\cong X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i$, one has $L_i \in \mathcal{GI}(S_{\mathfrak m_i}/t_i^3S_{\mathfrak m_i} )$.

label: c:restriction
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $I$ be a totally acyclic complex of injective $\Sigma^{-1}S$-modules.
The restriction $\mathrm{Mod}_{\Sigma^{-1}S} \to \mathrm{Mod}_S$ is exact and preserves injectives, since its left adjoint $\Sigma^{-1}(-)$ is exact.
For an injective $S$-module $E$, the module $\Sigma^{-1}E$ is injective over $\Sigma^{-1}S$, since $S$ is commutative Noetherian.
The adjunction $\mathrm{Hom}_S(E,I)\cong \mathrm{Hom}_{\Sigma^{-1}S}(\Sigma^{-1}E,I)$ proves that $S$ is totally acyclic over $S$.

label: c:lem:lift
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:lift}
The module $H_i$ is Gorenstein injective over $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$ and over $S$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $t_i^3$ is regular on $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$ and $L_i$ is Gorenstein injective over $S_{\mathfrak m_i}/t_i^3S_{\mathfrak m_i}$, \cite[Theorem~4.2]{BennisMahdou2010} gives $\mathrm{Gid}_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}L_i
=\mathrm{Gid}_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}/t_i^3S_{\mathfrak m_i}}L_i+1=1$.
Applying \cite[Lemma~2.5\textup{(3)}]{BennisMahdou2010} to
\[
0\longrightarrow L_i\longrightarrow E_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}(L_i)
\longrightarrow H_i\longrightarrow0
\]
gives $\mathrm{Gid}_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}H_i\leq\max\{0,1-1\}=0$.
Thus $H_i$ is Gorenstein injective over $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$, and hence is also Gorenstein injective over $S$ by Lemma~\ref{c:restriction}.

label: c:lem:lift-ext
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:lift-ext}
There is an isomorphism of $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$ modules
\[
0\ne\mathrm{Ext}_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}^1(\Omega_{\mathfrak m_i},H_i)\cong\mathrm{Ext}_{X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i}^2(\bigl(X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i^*\bigr),L_i).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: c:lem:lift-support
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:lift-support}
As an $S$-module, $H_i$ satisfies $\mathrm{Supp}_S(H_i)=\{\mathfrak m_i\}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $L_i$ is a module over $S_{\mathfrak m_i}/t_i^3S_{\mathfrak m_i}\cong X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i$, whose maximal ideal $(a,b,u,v)$ has cube zero, one has $(\mathfrak m_iS_{\mathfrak m_i})^3L_i=0$.
The socle of $L_i$ is an essential submodule of $L_i$.
Thus $E_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}(L_i)$ is a coproduct of copies of $E_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}(K_i)$.
Each copy is $\mathfrak m_i$-power torsion by \cite[Theorem~18.4(v)]{Matsumura1989}, so the quotient $H_i$ is also $\mathfrak m_i$-power torsion.
Hence $(H_i)_{\mathfrak q}=0$ for every prime $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m_i$.
Finally, $H_i\ne0$ by Lemma~\ref{c:lem:lift-ext}, and $(H_i)_{\mathfrak m_i}\cong H_i$.

label: c:lem:colimit-injective
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the set of compatible morphisms
\[
\Omega\longrightarrow
\Omega\otimes_B B[(t_i^3)^{-1}\mid i\in\mathbb N_+],
\qquad
x \longmapsto
\bigg({\prod_{j=1}^{n-1}a_j}\bigg)^{-1} \cdot x.
\]
The universal property of colimits yields a morphism
\[
\varinjlim\bigl(\Omega\xlongrightarrow{a_1}\Omega\xlongrightarrow{a_2}\Omega\longrightarrow\cdots\bigr) \longrightarrow \Omega\otimes_B B[(t_i^3)^{-1}\mid i\in\mathbb N_+].
\]
It it injective since each $a_i$ is injective and $B$ is an integral domain.
It is surjective since each element on the right hand side concerns only finite many $t_i$'s, thus admits a preimage.

Finally, $\Omega\otimes_BK\cong E_S(S/\mathfrak n)$ follows from Lemma~\ref{c:lem:genericinjective}.

label: c:lem:global-obstruction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{c:lem:global-obstruction}
Consider the tower
\[
\cdots\xlongrightarrow{a_3}\coprod_{i\geq1}\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)
\xlongrightarrow{a_2}\coprod_{i\geq1}\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)
\xlongrightarrow{a_1}\coprod_{i\geq1}\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i).
\]
Then one has $\varprojlim{}^1\coprod_{i\geq1}\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)\ne0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{c:lem:lift-ext}, $\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)
\cong\mathrm{Ext}_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}^1(\Omega_{\mathfrak m_i},H_i)\ne0$.
Since $X_i\otimes_{K_i}Y_i\cong S_{\mathfrak m_i}/t_i^3S_{\mathfrak m_i}$ is annihilated by $t^3$, one has $t_i^3\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)
\cong t_i^3\mathrm{Ext}_{S_{\mathfrak m_i}}^1(\Omega_{\mathfrak m_i},H_i)= 0$.

For $j\ne i$, multiplication by $t_j^3$ on this $S_{\mathfrak m_i}$-module is invertible. Consequently, $a_1\cdots a_{i-1}$ acts invertibly on $\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)$, whereas $(a_1\cdots a_i)\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)=0$.
For each $i \in \mathbb N_+$, fix $0\ne\xi_i\in\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i) \subseteq \coprod_i\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)$.
One gets a diagonal element
\[
(\xi_i)_{i\geq1}
\in\prod_{n\geq1}\coprod_{i\geq1}
\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i).
\]

We claim that $(\xi_i)_{i\geq1} \notin \mathrm{im}(1-\Delta)$, where $\Delta((y_i)_{i\geq 1})=(a_iy_{i+1})_{i \geq 1}$.
Otherwise, assume there were $(y_i)_{i\geq 1}$ with $y_i-a_iy_{i+1}=\xi_i$.
Iterating $y_i-a_i y_{i+1}=\xi_i$ gives
\[
y_1=\sum_{k=1}^m\left(\prod_{j=1}^{k-1}a_j\right)\xi_k
+\left(\prod_{j=1}^m a_j\right)y_{m+1}.
\]
In the $\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_m)$-component, all $\xi_k$ with $k\ne m$ vanish, and the last term vanishes since $t_m^3 \in \prod_{j=1}^m a_j$ is the annihilator.
Thus this component of $y_1$ equals $\left(\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}a_j\right)\xi_m\ne0$,
since every factor acts as an automorphism on $\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_m)$.
This holds for every $m$, contradicting the finite support of $y_1$.

Therefore, $(\xi_i)_{i\geq1}\notin\mathrm{im}(1-\Delta)$.
Thus $\mathrm{coker}(1-\Delta)
\cong\varprojlim{}^1\coprod_{i\geq1}\mathrm{Ext}_S^1(\Omega,H_i)\ne0$.
